questions.question: Why do some companies keep bees on their roofs?
choices: To show their concern for the environment.
To sell honey to their employees.
To help scientists with their research.
To reduce the number of wild bees.
questions.explanation: partly to show that they care about the environment と述べられている。

questions.question: What do experts recommend?
choices: Planting more flowers and trees in cities.
Banning beekeeping in large cities.
Moving beehives to the countryside.
Increasing the number of honeybees.
questions.explanation: 巣箱を増やすより花や木を植えることに力を入れるべきだと勧めている。

questions.question: What does the brain seem to do during deep sleep?
choices: Delete unnecessary memories.
Create new dreams from old memories.
Rest completely without any activity.
Replay information learned during the day.
questions.explanation: 深い眠りの間、日中に学んだ情報を再生しているようだと述べられている。

questions.question: What do researchers suggest about studying before exams?
choices: Students should study in the early morning.
Studying with friends improves memory.
Sleeping well may be better than studying all night.
Short naps are better than long sleep.
questions.explanation: 徹夜で勉強するより、ぐっすり眠るほうが効果的かもしれないと述べている。

questions.question: What is one reason night work may cause health problems?
choices: Night workers usually earn less money.
It disrupts the body's internal clock.
Night workers rarely exercise.
It is more physically demanding.
questions.explanation: 夜勤が体内時計(internal clock)を乱すことが理由の一つ。

questions.question: What do experts recommend for night-shift workers?
choices: Keeping a regular sleep schedule.
Eating a large meal at midnight.
Changing shifts as often as possible.
Sleeping only on their days off.
questions.explanation: 休日でも規則正しい睡眠スケジュールを守るよう勧めている。

questions.question: What causes coral bleaching?
choices: Pollution from ships.
Fishing with nets.
Water that is too warm.
A lack of sunlight.
questions.explanation: 水温が高くなりすぎるとサンゴが藻類を失い白化する。

questions.question: What do the scientists warn?
choices: Underwater nurseries harm fish.
Coral breeding is too expensive.
Global warming must be slowed to save reefs.
Reefs will recover on their own.
questions.explanation: 地球温暖化を遅らせない限り救えないと警告している。

questions.question: What do researchers say about standing all day?
choices: It is the best way to work.
It helps people lose weight quickly.
It can also cause health problems.
It improves concentration.
questions.explanation: 一日中立つのも脚や足に問題を起こすことがあると述べている。

questions.question: What do researchers recommend?
choices: Changing positions regularly.
Sitting for no more than four hours.
Using a standing desk all day.
Exercising before work.
questions.explanation: 定期的に姿勢を変えることを勧めている。

questions.question: What did the study find?
choices: Bored people performed tasks more slowly.
Bored people later had more creative ideas.
Smartphones improve creativity.
Children get bored more easily than adults.
questions.explanation: 退屈な作業をした参加者のほうが後でより独創的なアイデアを出した。

questions.question: What do the researchers suggest?
choices: People should use smartphones less at work.
Schools should give students more homework.
Adults should avoid boring tasks.
Children should sometimes be allowed to be bored.
questions.explanation: 特に子どもは、ときには退屈を感じることを許されるべきだと提案している。

questions.question: What is one reason people choose to live in tiny houses?
choices: To save money.
To live closer to the city center.
To have more possessions.
To avoid paying any taxes.
questions.explanation: 普通の家よりはるかに安いのでお金を節約したい人がいる。

questions.question: What problem do tiny house owners face?
choices: Moving their houses on wheels.
Finding legal places to put their houses.
Getting enough electricity.
Finding builders.
questions.explanation: 最小面積の規則があり、合法的に置ける場所を見つけるのが難しい。

questions.question: What is one cause of antibiotic resistance mentioned?
choices: Developing too many new drugs.
Using antibiotics for illnesses caused by viruses.
Patients refusing to take medicine.
A lack of hospitals.
questions.explanation: ウイルスが原因の風邪に抗生物質を処方するなどの使いすぎが原因とされている。

questions.question: What are health experts calling for?
choices: A complete ban on antibiotics.
Stricter rules on antibiotics in farming.
Fewer visits to doctors.
More farm animals.
questions.explanation: 農業での抗生物質使用の規則厳格化と新薬開発への投資を求めている。

questions.question: What is one criticism of volunteer tourism?
choices: It is too expensive for young people.
Volunteers rarely experience local culture.
Volunteers may take jobs from local workers.
The programs are too long.
questions.explanation: 地元の労働者の仕事を奪うことがあると批判されている。

questions.question: What do experts advise people to do?
choices: Volunteer only in their own country.
Choose programs that work with local communities.
Avoid working with children entirely.
Stay abroad for at least a year.
questions.explanation: 地域社会と協力して運営されているプログラムを選ぶよう助言している。

questions.question: What have some companies started?
choices: Early retirement programs.
Special training for managers.
Programs to hire only young people.
Mentoring programs led by older employees.
questions.explanation: 高齢の社員が若いスタッフに知識を伝える指導プログラムを始めた。

questions.question: What do experts say companies should do?
choices: Raise the retirement age.
Pay older workers more.
Reduce the number of older workers.
Offer flexible working hours.
questions.explanation: 柔軟な勤務時間(flexible working hours)を提供すべきだと述べている。

questions.question: What do participants do when they arrive at the camps?
choices: Hand over their devices.
Take a sleep test.
Set goals for their phone use.
Choose a roommate.
questions.explanation: 到着時に携帯電話などの機器を預ける。

questions.question: What do psychologists recommend?
choices: Attending a camp every month.
Buying a simpler phone.
Giving up smartphones completely.
Making small changes in daily life.
questions.explanation: 通知をオフにするなど、日常生活で小さな変化を起こすことを勧めている。

questions.question: What problem can planting trees on grasslands cause?
choices: It can destroy habitats for some animals and plants.
It increases the amount of carbon dioxide.
It makes the soil too wet for farming.
It attracts too many tourists.
questions.explanation: 自然の草原に木を植えると、開けた土地に頼る動植物のすみかを壊してしまうとある。

questions.question: What do experts say is often more effective?
choices: Planting billions of trees quickly.
Planting trees only on grasslands.
Cutting down old trees to plant new ones.
Protecting forests that already exist.
questions.explanation: 最後に、既存の森林を守るほうが効果的なことが多いと述べている。

questions.question: What did studies find about the lower speed limits?
choices: They had little effect on average travel times.
They caused serious traffic jams in Paris.
They increased noise in many neighborhoods.
They led to more traffic lights being installed.
questions.explanation: 渋滞を招くという批判に対し、研究では平均の移動時間はほとんど変わらなかったとある。騒音はむしろ下がった。

questions.question: What do experts say is necessary?
choices: Putting up more speed limit signs.
Raising fines for parking illegally.
Banning cars from city centers.
Making changes to the roads themselves.
questions.explanation: 標識だけでは不十分で、運転手が速度を出し続けた都市では道路を狭くし減速帯を設ける必要があったと述べている。

questions.question: What happened in some cities after transportation became free?
choices: Most drivers stopped using their cars.
Many new passengers had previously walked or cycled.
Low-income residents began to drive more.
The number of passengers went down.
questions.explanation: 乗客数は急増したが、新しい利用者の多くは車をやめた人ではなく、以前は歩いたり自転車に乗ったりしていた人だったとある。

questions.question: What do researchers suggest?
choices: All countries should follow Luxembourg's example.
Parking should be free in city centers.
Better service is more important than free fares.
Bicycles should be banned from busy streets.
questions.explanation: 無料にすることは、本数が多く信頼できるものにすることほど重要ではないと指摘し、サービス改善と駐車料金を勧めている。

questions.question: How is the Seabed 2030 project collecting data more quickly?
choices: By sending satellites to Mars.
By using equipment on ordinary boats.
By hiring more research scientists.
By laying new undersea cables.
questions.explanation: 調査船だけでなく、特別な機器を積むことに同意した漁船や個人のヨットからもデータを集めていると述べている。

questions.question: What concern do some environmental groups have?
choices: Maps may encourage deep-sea mining.
Fishing boats may damage the seafloor.
The project will not be finished on time.
Tsunamis may become harder to predict.
questions.explanation: 最後に、より良い地図によって企業が深海で採掘しやすくなるのではないかと懸念していると述べている。

questions.question: How do buy-now-pay-later services mainly make money?
choices: By charging stores a fee for each sale.
By charging customers high interest.
By selling customer data to banks.
By opening their own online stores.
questions.explanation: 主に売り上げ1件ごとに店から手数料を取ることで利益を得ているとある。利息はかからないことが多い。

questions.question: What are some governments doing?
choices: Banning online shopping for young people.
Forcing stores to stop offering discounts.
Requiring checks on whether customers can repay.
Limiting the number of items people can buy.
questions.explanation: 購入を承認する前に、客が返済できるかを確認するよう企業に義務づける規則を導入していると述べている。

questions.question: What did the experiment show?
choices: Reading a passage four times was the best method.
Students forgot most of the passage within a day.
Students in both groups remembered the same amount.
Students who tried to recall the passage remembered more.
questions.explanation: 1回読んで残りの時間を思い出すことに使ったグループのほうが、1週間後にはるかに多く覚えていたとある。

questions.question: What is surprising about the students who reread the passage?
choices: They spent less time studying.
They enjoyed the experiment more.
They were more confident about their performance.
They used flashcards to prepare.
questions.explanation: 成績は低かったのに、読み返したグループのほうが良い成績を取れると自信を持っていたと述べている(Interestingly 以下)。

questions.question: What is social jet lag?
choices: Tiredness caused by flying across time zones.
A sleep problem that affects only travelers.
The habit of taking naps in the afternoon.
A difference between weekday and weekend sleep schedules.
questions.explanation: 平日と週末の生活時間の差を社会的時差ぼけと呼ぶと説明している。旅行者の時差ぼけはたとえとして出てくるだけ。

questions.question: What do experts suggest people do on weekends?
choices: Go to bed later than on weekdays.
Take a short nap instead of sleeping late.
Stay in bed until they feel rested.
Travel to a different time zone.
questions.explanation: 週末に休息が必要なら、遅くまで寝るのではなく、午後に短い昼寝をするよう提案している。

questions.question: Why do supporters think compulsory voting is useful?
choices: It lowers the cost of running national elections.
It allows people to vote from home over the internet.
It makes politicians consider the views of a wider range of voters.
It guarantees that the same party always wins.
questions.explanation: 全員が投票すると、政治家は支持層だけでなく幅広い有権者に訴える必要が出る、というのが支持派の主張である。費用や投票方法の話は出てこない。

questions.question: What is one criticism of compulsory voting?
choices: It has made elections take place much less often.
It has caused most citizens to stop reading the news.
It allows only the richest citizens to become candidates.
Some people may vote randomly just to avoid a fine.
questions.explanation: 批判派は、候補者をよく知らない人が罰金を避けるためだけに適当に投票すると主張している。選挙の回数や候補者の資格については触れられていない。

questions.question: What benefit of geothermal heating is mentioned in the talk?
choices: Sidewalks can be kept free of snow without paying for snow removal.
It produces more electricity than wind power does.
It removes all harmful gases from the air.
It allows buildings to be built without foundations.
questions.explanation: レイキャビクでは温水で歩道の雪が溶け、雪かきの費用が省かれている。風力との比較や大気の浄化は本文にない。

questions.question: What is the risk of drilling deeper wells?
choices: It may cause the hot water to freeze.
It may trigger small earthquakes.
It may cause volcanoes to stop erupting.
It may make the energy supply too cheap to be profitable.
questions.explanation: 深く掘りすぎると小さな地震を誘発する危険がある、と述べられている。他の影響は本文に出てこない。

questions.question: What does the speaker say about quantum computers and everyday tasks?
choices: They are not faster than ordinary computers at everyday tasks.
They cannot connect to the internet at all.
They can only store numbers, not words.
They are too large to be moved into an office.
questions.explanation: 日常の作業では、量子コンピューターは普通のコンピューターより速いわけではないと説明されている。接続や保存の種類については触れられていない。

questions.question: Why must many quantum machines be kept at extremely low temperatures?
choices: Cold air makes their processors run faster than heat does.
Small changes in temperature or vibration can cause their qubits to make errors.
Low temperatures allow them to store more bits of information.
Cold conditions make the machines cheaper to manufacture.
questions.explanation: 量子ビットは非常にこわれやすく、温度や振動のわずかな変化で誤りが起きるため、極低温に保つ必要があると述べている。製造費や処理速度の話は出てこない。

questions.question: What is one theory about why hearing loss may be linked to dementia?
choices: The brain works so hard to decode sounds that less is left for memory.
Hearing loss directly damages the memory cells in the ears.
People with hearing loss always sleep less at night.
Hearing aids were found to speed up the decline in thinking ability.
questions.explanation: 脳が弱い音を聞き分けるのに多くの資源を使い、記憶に回す分が減るという説が紹介されている。耳の細胞が直接記憶を損なうという説明は本文にない。

questions.question: What does the speaker say about the large study of hearing aids?
choices: It proved that hearing aids cure dementia completely.
It found that hearing aids make hearing problems worse.
It cannot prove that hearing aids prevent dementia.
It showed that only wealthy people benefit from hearing aids.
questions.explanation: 補聴器を使う人は他の点でも違いがあるかもしれず、認知症を防ぐことは証明できないと述べている。治療効果や富裕層との関係は話題になっていない。

questions.question: Why do many well-known brands use pop-up shops?
choices: They are required by law to open a store for each new product.
They can charge much higher prices than in permanent stores.
They allow the company to avoid paying taxes altogether.
They can test products and create excitement at a low cost.
questions.explanation: ポップアップショップは、低い費用で新製品を試したり、発売を盛り上げたりするために使われると説明されている。法律上の義務や税金の話は出てこない。

questions.question: What is a risk of pop-up shops for small businesses?
choices: They must stay open for many years under the contract.
They are not allowed to sell products to shoppers.
They may not earn enough in a few weeks to cover their costs.
They have to hire more workers than they can afford.
questions.explanation: 小さな事業者は、数週間で費用を賄えるほどの利益を上げられないかもしれないと述べられている。契約期間や販売の禁止については触れられていない。

questions.question: Why do some people enjoy board games more than online games?
choices: They are cheaper than any other form of entertainment.
They require players to memorize long rulebooks before the first game.
They let players interact face to face in the same room.
They can be played only by young children.
questions.explanation: ボードゲームでは、同じ部屋で相手の表情を読み、話して笑い合えることが魅力だとされている。費用や対象年齢については触れられていない。

questions.question: What change has made modern board games easier to enjoy?
choices: They now have longer and more complicated rules.
They are sold only in video game stores.
They are played only in cafes and never at home.
They are shorter and easier to learn.
questions.explanation: デザイナーが現代のゲームを短く覚えやすくしたので、初心者が長い説明を聞かずに始められると説明されている。ルールが複雑になったという話はない。

questions.question: What did researchers find when they tested the learning styles theory carefully?
choices: Students did not learn better when lessons matched their supposed style.
Students learned best when they were taught only through pictures.
Students who used their preferred style scored much higher on tests.
Students forgot everything taught through physical activities.
questions.explanation: 慎重に検証すると、好みのスタイルに合わせた授業で生徒の成績が上がることはなかった。写真だけの授業や、好みのスタイルでの高得点は本文で示されていない。

questions.question: What does the speaker recommend educators focus on?
choices: Sorting students into groups based on their learning style.
Using more pictures and videos in every single lesson.
Giving students longer breaks between their classes.
Strategies such as quizzing oneself and spacing out study sessions.
questions.explanation: 教材の復習、自己テスト、学習の間隔をあけることなど、ほぼ全員に効果がある方法に集中すべきだと述べている。学習スタイルで生徒を分類することは勧められていない。

questions.question: How were the members of the assembly selected?
choices: By random selection among local residents
Through a national election
By applying for seats on the council
By choosing volunteers from political parties
questions.explanation: 「chosen by lottery」より、住民の中から無作為の抽選で選ばれた。選挙、応募、政党からの選出は本文にない。

questions.question: What will the town council do with the report?
choices: Build the new homes immediately
Ask the national government to cancel the plan
Hire the members as full-time staff
Read it carefully before making a decision
questions.explanation: 「read the report carefully before it makes a final decision」より、決定の前に報告書を注意深く読む。すぐに建設する、計画を取り消す、委員を職員として雇う、は本文にない。

questions.question: What did teachers notice after the recess was brought back?
choices: Students finished their homework faster.
Students asked for longer school days.
Teachers stopped giving any homework.
Children were calmer and more focused.
questions.explanation: 「the children were calmer and more focused」より、休み時間の復活後に子どもたちが落ち着いて集中するようになった。宿題が早く終わる、授業時間を延ばす、宿題をなくす、は本文にない。

questions.question: Who decided to bring back the recess?
choices: The parents of the students
The local government
The head teacher of the school
The school board
questions.explanation: 「the head teacher decided to bring back a fifteen-minute recess」より、休み時間を復活させたのは校長先生。保護者、地方自治体、教育委員会の決定は本文にない。

questions.question: What is the main purpose of rent control?
choices: To encourage landlords to build more apartments
To protect renters from sudden increases
To lower the cost of constructing new buildings
To reduce the number of families in large cities
questions.explanation: 家賃の値上げを制限して、借家人を守る制度だと説明されている。大家に建設を促す、建設費を下げる、大都市の家族を減らす、は本文にない。

questions.question: What do many economists suggest?
choices: Ending all limits on rent increases in cities
Encouraging families to move to rural towns
Building affordable housing while protecting long-term tenants
Banning the construction of new apartments
questions.explanation: 「a middle path」として、手頃な住宅を建てつつ長期の借家人を守ることを提案している。家賃規制の全廃、地方への移住、新しいアパートの建設禁止は本文にない。

questions.question: What do some companies now do instead of requiring degrees?
choices: They hire only graduates from famous universities
They evaluate what applicants can actually do
They offer degrees to their own employees
They stop interviewing candidates altogether
questions.explanation: 学位の代わりに、応募者が実際にできることを評価すると説明されている。名門大学の卒業生に限る、社員に学位を与える、面接をやめる、は本文にない。

questions.question: Why do the managers think the new approach is helpful?
choices: It saves money on job advertisements.
It makes interviews much shorter.
It reveals talented people they might have missed.
It lets applicants avoid taking any tests.
questions.explanation: 人事担当者は、従来なら見落とされた優秀な人を見つけられると話している。広告費、面接時間、テストの免除は本文にない。

questions.question: What did drivers complain about?
choices: The cameras were placed too far from the schools.
The fines were too small to change behavior.
The limits were set unfairly low in certain areas.
The map of the camera locations was never published.
questions.explanation: ドライバーは、制限速度が不必要に低く設定されていると不満を述べた。学校からの距離、罰金の額は不満として本文にない。地図は後に公開されている。

questions.question: Why does the spokesperson say that openness is necessary?
choices: Drivers always break rules unless they are fined.
Transparency helps people accept rules they believe are fair.
Fines are the only reliable way to improve safety.
The council should remove all cameras from the roads.
questions.explanation: 「a rule is only respected when people believe it was made fairly」より、公正だと信じられてこそ規則が守られるので、情報公開が必要だという理屈。ドライバーは罰金がないと規則を破る、罰金だけが方法、カメラを撤去すべき、は本文にない。

questions.question: How did the hospital monitor hand cleaning?
choices: By asking nurses to fill in weekly paper forms
By using devices that tracked sanitizer usage
By hiring extra staff to wash hands for others
By putting up new posters in every room
questions.explanation: 消毒液の使用を記録するセンサーを使った。ポスターは使わなかったと述べられている。週ごとの紙の記録、代わりに手を洗う人員の配置は本文にない。

questions.question: Why did the nurses find the monthly results helpful?
choices: The data showed that the sensors were working perfectly.
The data proved that other hospitals had failed.
The data reminded them of a habit they tended to neglect when busy.
The data let them compare their salaries with other staff.
questions.explanation: 「a routine that is easy to neglect under pressure」が根拠。忙しいときに忘れがちな習慣を思い出させたのが、結果の情報だと説明されている。センサーの完全な動作、他病院の失敗、給与の比較は本文にない。

questions.question: Why do the program's designers recommend testing the idea in cities?
choices: The payment did not meet the high living costs in urban areas.
Participants in the rural region had all stopped working.
Critics had proven that people always quit their jobs.
The national government had already approved the policy.
questions.explanation: 「not large enough to cover housing costs in the cities」より、都市の住居費に対して支給額が足りず、農村の結果が都市にも当てはまるか分からないため。働くのをやめた、批判者が証明した、政府がすでに承認した、は本文と合わない。

questions.question: What does the speaker imply about the results so far?
choices: They show that the policy should be introduced nationwide.
They are promising but do not yet prove the idea works.
They confirm that people stopped working once they received the payment.
They prove that rural families spend most of their money on housing.
questions.explanation: 「encouraging, though far from conclusive」より、結果は有望だが決定的ではないと考えている。全国導入、支給後の離職、農村の家族の住居費への支出は本文と合わない。

questions.question: Why are some bathhouses still able to attract visitors?
choices: They still serve as meeting places for local residents.
They have become cheaper than private bathrooms in new homes.
They have banned children from visiting the premises.
They offer more hot springs than any other spa in Japan.
questions.explanation: 「kept their original role as a meeting place」より、地域の人が集まる場としての役割を保った施設が成功していると説明されている。安さ、子どもの入場禁止、温泉の多さは本文にない。

questions.question: What does the speaker suggest about young visitors?
choices: They are attracted to a sense of peace that modern spas lack.
They are mainly interested in the low prices of old bathhouses.
They want to replace bathhouses with private bathrooms.
They hope to find jobs in the bathhouse business.
questions.explanation: 若い人は古い銭湯で、現代の温泉施設にはない落ち着きを感じると話している。安さへの関心、家庭の浴室への置き換え、就職の話は本文にない。

title: A downtown car ban that changed twice

questions.question: What is the city's current plan for downtown traffic?
choices: Ban private cars from downtown on weekdays.
Allow cars downtown only on weekends.
Keep the downtown area open to all traffic without changes.
Limit trucks to early hours and designate areas for unloading.
questions.explanation: 最終的に決まったのは、配送トラックを早朝に限り、荷下ろし用の区域を設けることだ。平日の車両禁止と週末だけの禁止は、いずれも途中で取り下げられた案。全面的な変更なしは本文と合わない。

questions.question: Why did officials drop the weekend-only plan?
choices: A study found that trucks, not cars, were responsible for the congestion.
Shop owners asked for a full ban on delivery trucks.
Residents asked for a full ban on cars all week long.
The city lacked the funds needed to install new signs.
questions.explanation: 交通調査で、渋滞の主な原因は自家用車ではなく配送トラックだと分かり、週末だけの案が取り下げられた。店主の要求、住民が全日の車両禁止を求めた、財源不足は本文にない。

title: A battery claim that was withdrawn

questions.question: What is the team's current view of its battery material?
choices: It can charge electric cars in just a few minutes.
It is ready for mass production in cars.
Independent laboratories have confirmed its performance.
It could be practical only for tiny gadgets, not vehicles.
questions.explanation: 「useful, but only for small devices such as sensors」より、小型の機器に限って役立つ可能性がある。急速充電の主張は撤回され、車への量産は本文で見通せていない。独立機関による確認はなかった。

questions.question: Why did the team withdraw its original claim?
choices: Investors demanded that the team stop its research.
The government banned all research on battery materials.
Companies complained that the plan was too expensive.
A mistake in its measurements had made the data look more promising.
questions.explanation: 測定の誤りによって元のデータが実際より良く見えていたと、チームが認めたことが理由。投資家の要求、政府の禁止、企業の不満は本文にない。

title: A local currency in a seaside town

questions.question: Where can the local currency be spent?
choices: Only at businesses located in the town
At any large chain across the country
Only at online stores in other cities
At government offices in the capital
questions.explanation: 地元の店でしか使えないと説明されている。大手チェーン店や他都市の店では使えない。全国の店、ネット店舗、首都の役所は本文にない。

questions.question: Who issues the currency?
choices: The national government
A large bank in another city
The shop owners' association
A small nonprofit organization
questions.explanation: 小さな非営利団体が発行していると述べられている。国、他都市の大手銀行、商店の組合は本文にない。

questions.question: When will construction begin?
choices: Immediately after the next election
Two years from now
Right after the public meeting
Sometime in the coming spring
questions.explanation: 工事は今度の春に始まる予定だと述べられている。次の選挙の直後、2年後、住民説明会の直後は本文にない。

questions.question: What is the main concern of some drivers?
choices: That the bike lane will be too narrow
That cyclists will refuse to use the lane
That parking spaces will be lost
That the river will become polluted
questions.explanation: 一部のドライバーは駐車スペースが減ることを心配している。ただし市は減るのはわずかだと説明している。車線の幅、自転車の利用、川の汚染は本文にない。

questions.question: What do some studies show about children who start early?
choices: They always outperform older learners in grammar.
They tend to speak with better pronunciation.
They quit learning the language by their teens.
They learn to read the language before speaking it.
questions.explanation: 早く始めた子どもは発音のレベルが高くなる傾向があると述べられている。文法で常に上回るという主張は、文法では優位が続かないとの記述と合わない。

questions.question: What do teachers suggest schools should focus on?
choices: Starting language lessons at a younger age
Testing children's grammar every single week
Giving students regular chances to practice
Hiring more teachers from abroad
questions.explanation: 早く始めることよりも、定期的に練習する機会を与えることに集中すべきだと教師は提案している。早期開始は勧められていない。毎週の文法テスト、外国人教師の採用は本文にない。

title: Disaster drills in a coastal city

questions.question: What has the city added to this year's drill?
choices: Free meals for all elderly residents
Each household writing a personal evacuation route
Higher prizes for the best volunteers
A drill held in the middle of the night
questions.explanation: 今年から、各家庭が自宅の避難経路を書き出して家族と話し合うことが加わった。無料の食事、ボランティアへの賞、夜間の訓練は本文にない。

questions.question: What is the mayor's main point?
choices: The drills should be cancelled because they are too costly.
Volunteers should be paid for their work.
Preparing at home is just as important as community efforts.
Public shelters are no longer needed in the city.
questions.explanation: 家庭での備えは、地域の取り組みと同じくらい大切だと市長は考えている。訓練の中止、ボランティアへの報酬、避難所が不要になるという話は本文にない。

questions.question: What advantage do subscriptions give to companies?
choices: They allow customers to buy programs in boxes again.
They reduce the need to improve their products.
They provide predictable revenue that supports long-term planning.
They let customers pay once for a permanent license.
questions.explanation: 定期的な収入が入るので、先の計画を立てやすく、製品の改良にも役立つ。箱入りでの販売や一度払いの買い切りは以前の方式として出てくるだけで、利点ではない。製品の改良が不要になるという話もない。

questions.question: Why do consumer advocates recommend reviewing subscriptions regularly?
choices: Because cancelling a subscription always leads to large fines.
Because people may keep paying for services they seldom need.
Because most companies stop offering subscriptions after a year.
Because subscriptions are cheaper than buying programs in boxes.
questions.explanation: 使わないサービスに料金を払い続けてしまうおそれがあるため、定期的な見直しを勧めている。解約の罰金、1年で終わる定額制、箱入りより安い、は本文にない。

questions.question: How did many residents in the recent survey feel about the groups?
choices: They believed the groups had eliminated all burglaries.
They felt more uneasy than secure.
They wanted the groups to report suspicious people to the police.
They thought the groups should meet only during the summer.
questions.explanation: 調査では、多くの住民が見守りグループによって安心よりも不安を感じたと答えた。空き巣がなくなった、警察への通報を求めた、夏だけ活動すべきだという話は、住民の感想として本文にない。

questions.question: What do the organizers imply about close relationships between neighbors?
choices: They make watching the streets unnecessary in every case.
They mean that residents should stop reporting anything to the police.
They make people more willing to ask others for assistance.
They make it easier to judge people by their background.
questions.explanation: 近所の人を知っている人ほど、困ったときに助けを求めやすいと主催者は述べている。見張りが不要になる、警察への通報をやめる、背景で判断する、は本文の内容と逆か、本文にない。

questions.question: Why have some hospitals stopped their therapy-dog programs?
choices: Some incidents raised doubts about the safety of the visits.
Patients were too frightened of the animals to continue.
The dogs refused to visit patients recovering from surgery.
Because the dogs had stopped reducing patients' stress.
questions.explanation: 感染のリスクへの懸念と、いくつかの事故を受けて、一部の病院がプログラムを中止したと説明されている。患者の恐怖、犬の拒否、ストレスを減らさなくなったことは本文にない(本文では減らすと言われている)。

questions.question: What does the speaker suggest about the value of therapy dogs?
choices: They are more effective than any medicine for treating infections.
Their comfort may be genuine, though hospitals must weigh it against dangers.
They should be banned from all hospitals because of their risks.
They work best when they are kept away from patients.
questions.explanation: 犬がもたらす安らぎは本物かもしれないが、病院は危険と比べて判断しなければならないと述べている。感染症の治療薬より効果がある、全面的に禁止すべき、患者から離すほうがよい、は本文と合わない。

questions.question: According to psychologists, why do students often delay their tasks?
choices: They try to escape uncomfortable emotions linked to the task.
They are not clever enough to finish their assignments early.
They prefer deadlines that are very close together.
They perform better when they feel rushed at the last minute.
questions.explanation: 心理学者によると、課題に対する退屈さや不安といった不快な感情を避けようとするのが先延ばしの原因。頭の良さ、締め切りの近さを好むこと、直前に急ぐと力が出ることは、本文では否定されているか述べられていない。

questions.question: What does the speaker suggest teachers should do?
choices: Ask students to create specific, concrete plans for their work.
Remind students about deadlines more often than before.
Give students longer deadlines so that they feel less pressure.
Reward students who finish their work at the last moment.
questions.explanation: 締め切りの通知だけでなく、具体的な計画を立てさせると生徒の成果が上がると述べている。締め切りを頻繁に知らせる、期限を延ばす、直前に終えた生徒を褒める、は勧められていない。

questions.question: What will visitors see in the main hall this autumn?
choices: The original scrolls displayed for longer hours
A small room with controlled lighting
The exhibition with extended opening hours
Accurate reproductions rather than the original scrolls
questions.explanation: 館内の主会場では、原本ではなく高品質の複製が展示される。原本は光を管理した小さな部屋に限って展示される。展示時間の延長は当初の計画で、取り下げられた案。

questions.question: Why was the exhibition of the original scrolls postponed?
choices: They were judged too delicate to be transported.
The autumn weather was too damp for displays.
Critics demanded a higher admission price.
Visitors had asked for copies rather than originals.
questions.explanation: 保存担当者が、巻物は移動に耐えられないほど傷みやすいと判断し、展示が延期された。天候、入場料、来館者の要望は本文にない。

title: A sports center that got smaller

questions.question: What option has the council now chosen?
choices: A new center on the riverside, as first planned
A new site on the former factory land
A new arena built on the hills
Upgrading the gymnasium at the local school
questions.explanation: 議会が選んだのは、学校の既存の体育館を改修し、小さな増築を加える案。川沿いの計画、工場跡地の計画は取り下げられた。丘の上の新しい競技場は本文にない。

questions.question: Why was the factory site dropped?
choices: Residents preferred a location on the riverside.
The council wanted a much larger sports arena instead.
Sports fans demanded a different kind of sport.
Its soil was found to be polluted and too costly to clean.
questions.explanation: 工場跡地は汚染されていることが分かり、浄化の費用が予算に対して高すぎたため。川沿いを望む住民の声は、むしろ川沿いの計画への反対だった。大きな競技場、別の競技を求めるファンは本文にない。

questions.question: What do stories help children learn?
choices: New vocabulary and how sentences are built
How to write their own picture books
How to play musical instruments
How to count money quickly
questions.explanation: 物語は新しい語彙と文のつくりを学ぶ助けになると述べられている。自分で絵本を書く、楽器の演奏、お金の数え方は本文にない。

questions.question: What kind of reading is most helpful?
choices: Reading silently by themselves every night
Reading only textbooks during school lessons
Reading only before the children go to bed
Reading that feels calm and fun
questions.explanation: くつろいで楽しめる読み聞かせが、もっとも効果的だと述べられている。黙読、教科書の読解、寝る前だけの読み聞かせは本文にない。

questions.question: What is the sensor designed to measure?
choices: The temperature of the air
The brightness of sunlight
The speed of the wind
How wet the soil is
questions.explanation: 土の中の水分を測るセンサーだと説明されている。空気の温度、日光の明るさ、風速は本文にない。

questions.question: When will the device be available?
choices: Starting this month
Only after the crops are harvested
Sometime in the coming year
It has been cancelled
questions.explanation: 今後1年以内に発売される予定だと述べられている。今月からの発売、収穫後の販売、中止は本文にない。

questions.question: What have the young council members proposed?
choices: Higher taxes on all public events
Additional bike parking by stations and a skating area
Free tickets for all elderly residents
The removal of every public park
questions.explanation: 若い委員は、駅の近くの自転車駐車場の増設と、空き地のスケートエリアを提案した。公共イベントへの増税、高齢者への無料券、公園の撤去は本文にない。

questions.question: What do supporters say the councils help young people do?
choices: Gain real authority over adult politicians
Earn money from city budgets
Understand how the government operates
Avoid taking part in public events
questions.explanation: 支持者は、この経験で若者が政府の仕組みを学べると述べている。本当の権限を得る、予算から収入を得る、イベントに参加しない、は本文にない。権限がないという指摘は批判する側の主張である。

questions.question: What did the markets originally sell?
choices: Imported spices for restaurants in the capital
Fresh seafood and produce for local homes
Cooked meals for tourists
Handmade pottery for travelers
questions.explanation: もとは近くの家庭向けに魚や野菜を売っていたと述べられている。首都の飲食店向けの香辛料、観光客向けの調理済みの食事(後に始まったもの)、旅人向けの陶器は本文にない。

questions.question: What are the markets known for today?
choices: Expensive restaurants with quiet dining rooms
Factories that produce fish for export
Small stalls where food is cooked in front of buyers
Large supermarkets with long opening hours
questions.explanation: 客の目の前で料理を焼く小さな屋台で知られていると述べられている。高級な食堂、輸出用の工場、大型スーパーは本文にない。

questions.question: What do researchers say the brain actually does when a person multitasks?
choices: It performs both demanding tasks at the same time.
It focuses only on phone notifications.
It alternates rapidly between demanding activities.
It stops working until the music ends.
questions.explanation: 研究者によると、脳は二つの作業を同時にこなすのではなく、その間を行ったり来たりしている。同時に処理する、通知だけに集中する、音楽が終わるまで止まる、は本文と合わない。

questions.question: What does the speaker mean by saying that 'the idea is not to punish students'?
choices: Students should never be allowed to use phones during class.
Teachers want to help students focus rather than discipline them.
Students who use phones should lose their class points.
Teachers should take away students' phones permanently.
questions.explanation: 「The idea is not to punish students」の後で、集中する機会を与えるのが狙いだと続けている。いつも使用禁止にすること、点数を減らすこと、スマホを永久に取り上げることは、本文の趣旨と違う。

questions.question: What do supporters say the wage increase will allow workers to do?
choices: Take on more hours at small restaurants
Pay for basic needs without relying on government help
Start their own restaurants more easily
Retire earlier than they had planned
questions.explanation: 支持者は、低賃金の労働者が公的な支援に頼らずに基本的な生活費をまかなえるようになると主張している。小さな飲食店での労働時間の増加、飲食店の開業のしやすさ、早期退職は本文にない。

questions.question: What does the speaker imply about the effect of the wage rise in different regions?
choices: It will affect all regions in exactly the same way.
It will matter most in areas where wages are already high.
It will depend heavily on the economic situation of each area.
It will be cancelled after the first year everywhere.
questions.explanation: 経済の状況は地域によって違い、その影響も地域ごとに違うと述べている。どの地域も同じ影響、賃金が高い地域で最も大きい、全国で一年後に廃止、はいずれも本文と合わない。

questions.question: Why do many couriers feel that the flexibility does not give them real freedom?
choices: They must work long hours just to earn enough money.
Their hours are assigned by the cities where they live.
Their pay is guaranteed for every delivery they make.
They prefer short shifts that fit around studies and parenting.
questions.explanation: 多くの配達員は、望む時間を選べず、目標の収入に届くまで長時間働いている。そのため柔軟性は本当の自由ではないと感じている。市による時間の割り当て、支払いの保証、短時間勤務の好みは、本文と合わない、または企業側の主張である。

questions.question: What does the speaker suggest about the platform owners' objection to new rules?
choices: They believe couriers should be paid directly by customers.
They prioritize lower costs over couriers' security.
They think the rules will increase the number of jobs.
They have already agreed to pay a guaranteed minimum for each delivery.
questions.explanation: プラットフォーム側は、ルールが導入されると客の料金が上がり、仕事の数が減ると恐れている。つまり、配達員の保障より費用を抑えることを重視していると読める。客による直接の支払い、仕事の増加、既に最低保証を約束したことは本文と合わない。

questions.question: Why might research on edited crops be slowed down?
choices: Regulations classify them the same way as other modified foods.
Farmers refuse to grow any new varieties of crops.
The technique cannot change the genes of plants at all.
Consumers have already banned all research on food.
questions.explanation: 編集された作物を遺伝子組み換え食品と同じ厳しい規制で扱う国があり、そのため研究が遅れると述べられている。農家が栽培を拒む、遺伝子を変えられない、消費者が研究を禁止した、は本文と合わない。

questions.question: What does the speaker imply about public acceptance of edited crops?
choices: It depends as much on communication as on the technology itself.
It is guaranteed once farmers report higher yields.
It has nothing to do with how the risks are explained.
It is mostly determined by the cost of the technique.
questions.explanation: 科学者は、技術そのものと同じくらい、リスクや利点をどのように伝えるかが大切だと述べている。収穫量が増えれば受け入れられる、説明は無関係、費用で決まる、は本文と合わない。

questions.question: What is the council's final decision about the pool?
choices: It will be closed during the summer to save money.
It will be run by a private company.
It will open only on weekends with reduced hours.
It will stay fully open after using a national grant for repairs.
questions.explanation: 最終的に議会は、全国の補助金を使って屋根を修理し、プールを全面的に開け続けることにした。夏の閉鎖、民間企業への委託、週末だけの営業は、いずれも途中で取り下げられた案。

questions.question: Why was the plan to hand the pool to a private company dropped?
choices: The building turned out to need costly repairs.
The company was unwilling to hire any local staff.
The council found the pool was too small to be profitable.
Parents asked for longer summer hours at the pool.
questions.explanation: 民間企業は、建物に高額な修理が必要だと分かった後に申し出を撤回した。現地採用を嫌がった、採算が取れない規模だった、夏の営業時間の延長を親が求めた、は本文にない。

questions.question: What should doctors tell patients about the supplement now?
choices: It has been proven to improve sleep in large trials.
It is safe to recommend because the manufacturer says it works.
It can replace prescribed medicine for sleep problems.
The evidence supporting it is not yet adequate.
questions.explanation: 医師は、このサプリの根拠は現時点では不十分だと患者に伝えるよう勧められている。大規模な試験で効果が証明された、製造元が効くと言うから安全に勧められる、処方薬の代わりになる、は本文と合わない。

questions.question: Why did officials ask clinics to stop recommending the supplement?
choices: The manufacturer refused to pay for a second trial.
Patients complained that the supplement tasted terrible.
The first study had been published in a famous journal.
A bigger independent study did not find a real benefit.
questions.explanation: より大きな独立した試験で、サプリと偽薬のあいだに意味のある差が見られなかったため、追加の試験が終わるまで勧めないよう求められた。製造元が試験費用を拒んだ、味への苦情、有名な雑誌への掲載は本文と合わない。

questions.question: What were early calendars based on?
choices: The phases of the moon
The seasons of the ocean
The height of mountains
The growth of forests
questions.explanation: 初期の暦は月を基にしていたと述べられている。海の季節、山の高さ、森の成長は本文にない。

questions.question: Why did farmers need a reliable calendar?
choices: To pay taxes to the rulers
To record the births of their children
To celebrate festivals in the capital
To know the right time to plant crops
questions.explanation: 作物をいつ植えるかを知るために、信頼できる暦が必要だったと歴史家は述べている。税金、出生の記録、祭りは本文にない。

questions.question: What do customers receive when they return the containers?
choices: A free loaf of bread every day
A new reusable bag
A cash refund at the register
A small discount on their next purchase
questions.explanation: 容器を返すと、次回の購入で少し値引きされると述べられている。毎日無料のパン、新しい袋、レジでの現金返金は本文にない。

questions.question: What does the owner hope will happen?
choices: The bakery will close the shopping street
Customers will stop buying bread altogether
Other shops will adopt the same idea
The city will ban plastic bags forever
questions.explanation: 店主は、商店街の他の店も同じ取り組みを始めることを望んでいる。店が通りを閉める、客がパンを買わなくなる、市がビニール袋を永久に禁止する、は本文にない。

questions.question: What did the study of older adults find?
choices: Walking long distances was the only useful exercise.
Regular, moderate walking was linked to fewer heart problems.
Only people who could run fast benefited from walking.
Walking caused more heart problems among older adults.
questions.explanation: 高齢者を対象にした研究では、適度な歩行を定期的に行うと心臓の病気のリスクが低いとされた。長距離歩行だけが役立つ、速く走れる人だけが得をする、歩行で心臓病が増えた、は本文にない。

questions.question: What do doctors recommend for people who cannot walk far?
choices: Staying in bed to save their energy
Walking very fast for at least one hour
Getting up often and taking brief walks each day
Standing still for long periods of time
questions.explanation: 遠くまで歩くのが難しい人も、立ち上がって一日を通して短い散歩を重ねれば効果があると医師は述べている。ベッドで休む、一時間以上速く歩く、長時間立ち続けるは本文にない。

questions.question: Why do the struggling students feel more comfortable?
choices: They are paid for attending the lunch sessions.
They find it less intimidating to ask questions in small groups.
They can skip the regular lessons entirely.
They can ask the teacher during every lesson.
questions.explanation: 大きな授業より、質問しやすいと感じている。少人数のグループでは、質問への気後れが少ないという意味。昼食時の報酬、授業の免除、毎回の質問機会は本文にない。

questions.question: What did the tutors discover?
choices: Their classmates usually refuse to listen to them.
Lunch breaks are too short for any lessons.
Teaching an idea helps them understand it more clearly.
Teachers prefer to work alone on lessons.
questions.explanation: ある考えを説明すると、自分自身の理解が明確になると、チューターは気づいた。クラスメートが話を聞かない、昼休みが短すぎる、教師が一人で授業を準備したがる、は本文にない。

questions.question: How do the new AI systems produce their forecasts?
choices: By simulating the physics of every storm
By asking meteorologists to predict each day manually
By learning from records of earlier weather
By measuring winds with satellites only
questions.explanation: 新しいAIシステムは、何十年分もの過去のデータから学習して予報を作る。大気の物理を計算するのは従来の方式で、人が手作業で予測する、衛星だけで風を測る、は本文にない。

questions.question: What does the speaker suggest about the weakness of AI forecasts?
choices: They are less accurate than traditional forecasts for common weather.
They may overlook uncommon storms because such cases were rarely recorded.
They cannot forecast anything beyond a single day.
They always predict storms more often than necessary.
questions.explanation: AIは、学習データに少ない稀な出来事、たとえば突然の嵐を見逃すことがあると指摘している。よくある天気での精度が低い、一日以上の予報ができない、嵐を多く予測しすぎる、は本文と合わない。

questions.question: Where were early confectionery shops often found?
choices: Beside the markets where sugar-coated snacks were sold
Close to religious sites
In busy harbors where traders gathered
At the top of mountain roads used by travelers
questions.explanation: 菓子店は寺の近くにあり、参拝者に砂糖をまぶした菓子を売っていたと述べられている。市場の隣、港、山道の上は本文にない。

questions.question: Why do customers keep returning to the oldest shops?
choices: The buildings are the most modern in the area.
The prices are lower than at newer stores.
The flavors evoke memories from their early years.
The shops have recently opened branches in every city.
questions.explanation: 客は、味が子どもの頃の思い出を呼び起こすから戻ってくると、店主は話している。建物が新しいから、値段が安いから、支店が増えたから、は本文にない。

questions.question: According to the speaker, what do some people argue about programs open to everyone?
choices: They help children from different backgrounds build bonds over shared meals.
They are cheaper than programs that target low-income families.
They make it unnecessary to fund any school meals at all.
They guarantee healthier meals than lunches brought from home.
questions.explanation: 誰でも利用できる制度には、異なる背景の子どもが一緒に食べて交流できるという社会的効果があると、一部の人は主張している。費用が安い、学校給食が不要になる、家庭の弁当より健康的、は本文と合わない。

questions.question: What does the speaker suggest about the best policy?
choices: Universal lunches are always fairer than targeted ones.
It depends on how each town chooses to design its program.
Discounted lunches should be abolished in all towns.
Free lunches are cheaper for families than home-cooked meals.
questions.explanation: 研究者の意見は分かれており、結果は各自治体がプログラムをどう設計するかに大きく左右される、と述べている。誰でも利用できる制度が常に公平、割引制度の全廃、家庭の手作り弁当より安い、は本文と合わない。

questions.question: According to the speaker, why do many old family firms get through difficult periods?
choices: Their cautious finances and focused craft, along with staff loyalty, help them endure hard times.
They borrow money whenever markets collapse.
They change their main product every few years.
They hire managers from outside the family only.
questions.explanation: 借金を避け、一つの技や製品に集中し、従業員の忠誠心を保っていることが、困難な時期を乗り越える理由だと研究者は述べている。市場の崩壊時に借金する、製品を数年ごとに変える、家族以外の経営者だけを採用する、は本文と合わない。

questions.question: What does the speaker suggest about the future of these family-run firms?
choices: They must balance their traditions with openness to change.
They should give up their traditions to compete with newer firms.
They will certainly fail once the founders retire.
They should hire only relatives to protect their loyalty.
questions.explanation: 長期的な価値観を守りつつ、新しい考えを受け入れる姿勢が必要だと専門家は勧めている。伝統を捨てる、創業者の引退後は必ず失敗する、親族だけを採用する、は本文と合わない。

questions.question: What has the school finally decided about its start time?
choices: Start classes at nine every day.
Start at eight thirty on most days.
Start at nine only on Wednesdays.
Keep the eight o'clock start, but let approved students arrive later.
questions.explanation: 最終的に、全員の始業は8時のままとし、医療上の理由で睡眠が必要な生徒は、教師の承認を得て9時に登校してよいことになった。9時の全日始業、8時半の始業、水曜だけ9時の案は、いずれも取り下げられた案。

questions.question: Why was the Wednesday-only plan abandoned?
choices: Transportation companies could not adjust for a single day.
Parents strongly opposed a later start on Wednesdays.
Teachers refused to teach on Wednesdays.
The school lacked enough classrooms for the change.
questions.explanation: 地元のバス会社が、週に1日だけダイヤを変えられないと述べたため、水曜日だけの計画は取り下げられた。保護者の強い反対、教師の授業拒否、教室不足は本文にない。

questions.question: According to the doctors, what is the most reliable option for chronic back pain?
choices: The few-session treatment that the clinic advertises
Results from the clinic's own patient surveys
Treatments offered at the clinic's three branches
An exercise plan with a professional overseeing it
questions.explanation: 医師は、監督付きの運動プログラムが、もっとも裏付けのある選択肢だと述べている。クリニックが宣伝する数回の治療、クリニック独自の患者調査の結果、三つの支店での治療は、いずれも本文の結論ではない。

questions.question: Why did the agency tell the clinic to stop its advertising?
choices: Patients demanded a refund for their treatments.
The treatment cost more than standard exercise programs.
Other clinics complained about the new branches.
Its quick-results claim was not backed by independent findings.
questions.explanation: 独立機関の検討で、少ない回数で効くという主張を裏付けるデータが、クリニック自身の調査に頼っていることが分かったため。返金の要求、治療費の比較、他院の苦情は本文にない。

title: Where to put a new city hall

questions.question: What did the council finally decide to do?
choices: Construct a new building where the old one stood.
Build a new city hall on farmland outside town.
Rent offices inside a downtown shopping mall.
Move its departments permanently into a former school.
questions.explanation: 「In the end, the council voted to rebuild on the original site in the city center」とあり、最終的には元の場所に建て直すことになった。町はずれの農地に建てる案と、ショッピングモールを借りる案は、どちらも却下された案。かつての学校は「temporary offices ... for three years」とあるように一時的な移転先で、恒久的に移るわけではない。

questions.question: Why was the shopping mall plan rejected?
choices: Residents could only reach the mall easily by car.
The building might not be open whenever the city needed it.
The rent was higher than the cost of new construction.
Shop owners refused to share their space with city staff.
questions.explanation: 「the city could not guarantee access to the building outside the mall's business hours」とあり、営業時間外に建物を使えないおそれがあったため却下された。車でなければ行きにくいというのは、農地の案に対する住民の反対理由。家賃が建設費より高い、店主が場所の共有を拒んだ、は本文にない。

questions.question: What does the speaker say about the accuracy of the volunteers' counts?
choices: They are too unreliable to be used in serious scientific studies.
They reflect general patterns well but can overlook uncommon birds.
They are more precise than the counts made by professional experts.
They became accurate only after hunters joined the project.
questions.explanation: 「the overall trends matched closely, although beginners did tend to miss rare species」をまとめると、全体の傾向は正しく表すが珍しい鳥を見落とすことがある、となる。科学に使えないほど不正確というのは、当初の「some researchers doubted」で、後の研究で否定された内容。専門家より正確、狩猟をする人が加わってから正確になった、は本文にない。

questions.question: What concern do the organizers have about the project's future?
choices: Photos of unusual birds are becoming difficult to verify.
Birds may soon move too far north to be counted at all.
It may struggle to attract enough participants in coming years.
Experienced volunteers are unwilling to train new members.
questions.explanation: 「the project depends entirely on people giving up their free time」と「few younger people have joined in recent years and ... the average age of participants keeps rising」をつなぐと、将来、十分な参加者を集められなくなるおそれがあると分かる。写真の確認が難しい、鳥が北へ移りすぎて数えられない、経験者が新人の指導を嫌がる、は本文にない。

title: Saving a mountain town's harvest festival

questions.question: What has the committee finally decided about the procession?
choices: The shrines will travel on carts, with student helpers allowed.
The procession will be held on just one of the two days.
Paid carriers from other areas will carry the heavy shrines.
Only elders will be allowed to take part in the procession.
questions.explanation: 「the shrines will be moved on lighter wheeled carts, and students from a nearby university who join the town's preservation society will be allowed to help」が最終的な合意。1日に短縮する案は商店主の抗議で撤回され、外部の専門の担ぎ手を雇う案は長老の反対で採用されなかった。長老だけが参加できる、は本文にない。

questions.question: Why was the plan to shorten the festival withdrawn?
choices: Elders insisted that only local people should carry the shrines.
Young residents offered to carry the shrines after all.
The festival was moved to a different weekend in autumn.
Businesses relied on the visitors who came on the second day.
questions.explanation: 「Local shop owners protested, saying the second day brought in most of their visitors, so that plan was withdrawn」とあり、商店が2日目の客に頼っていたため撤回された。地元の人だけが担ぐべきだというのは、外部の担ぎ手を雇う案に対する長老の反対理由。若者が結局担ぐと申し出た、別の週末に移した、は本文にない。

questions.question: What does the speaker say about the evidence for social prescribing?
choices: Its advantages appear more modest than early reports suggested.
It has been shown to replace medicine for most patients.
Larger studies found that it brought no benefits at all.
It works best for patients who have serious illnesses.
questions.explanation: 初期の報告(「patients who joined such activities visited their doctors less often」)に対し、「More recent studies with larger groups have found smaller benefits, though still positive ones」とあり、効果は当初の報告より控えめだと分かる。大規模な研究で効果がまったくなかった、は「still positive ones」で否定されている。多くの患者で薬の代わりになる、重い病気の患者に最も効く、は本文と合わない。

questions.question: Why do some health officials want community groups funded from the health budget?
choices: Doctors are refusing to prescribe medicine to lonely patients.
Programs fail where there are too few local activities to join.
Community groups currently charge patients very high fees.
Gardening clubs have proven more effective than any drug.
questions.explanation: 「the programs work only when local communities have enough clubs and volunteers, which is often not the case in poorer areas」を受けて「For this reason」と続くので、参加できる地域の活動が足りない所では取り組みが機能しないことが理由。医師が薬の処方を拒んでいる、団体が高い料金を取っている、ガーデニングがどの薬よりも効く、は本文にない。

questions.question: What rule is currently in effect for the scooters?
choices: They are banned from all of the city's streets entirely.
Each company may run only a limited number of them.
They must be left only in specially marked parking areas.
They may be used only by commuters during rush hour.
questions.explanation: 「Under the rules now in force, scooters may be parked only in marked zones」とあり、現在は指定区域にだけ止められる。全面禁止は採決前に見送られた案で、各社の台数の上限は後に取りやめになった案。通勤時間帯に通勤者だけが使える、は本文にない。

questions.question: Why did the council decide against a complete ban?
choices: Companies threatened to move scooters to the busiest areas.
Pedestrians said the scooters were no longer a problem.
Injury data showed that scooters were safer than cars.
Evidence showed that riders were making fewer short car trips.
questions.explanation: 「a transport study showed that many riders had stopped driving for short trips, so the ban was put aside」とあり、利用者が短い移動で車を使わなくなったという調査結果が理由。各社が混雑地域に移すと言ったのは、台数の上限の案が取りやめになった理由。歩行者がもう問題ないと言った、は本文にない。けがのデータは来年そろう予定で、まだ出ていない。

questions.question: What does the speaker suggest about the critics' concern?
choices: It is unlikely to be a serious problem because of how the system works.
It was shown to be correct after many false warnings had been sent.
It led researchers to stop collecting data from phones in large cities.
It has made professional seismic stations more expensive to build.
questions.explanation: 「Critics initially argued that phones would produce too many false alarms」に続けて「However, the system only reacts when hundreds of phones shake together, which rarely happens by chance」と言っている。2つをつなぐと、システムの仕組みのために誤報の心配は大きな問題にならないとわかる。誤報が多く出て正しいと分かったという内容は「However」で否定されている。都市の端末を使うのをやめた、観測所が高くなった、という話はない。

questions.question: What is one limitation of the system?
choices: Its warnings for quakes far from cities may come with little time to react.
Phone sensors are unable to feel the first, weaker waves of a quake.
It costs more to run than a network of professional seismic stations.
It sends too many alarms when people drop or run with their phones.
questions.explanation: 「phones are mostly concentrated in cities」と「warnings for earthquakes that begin in remote mountains or under the sea may arrive later, when there is little time left to act」をつなぐと、都市から遠い地震では警報が遅れ、行動する時間が少ないことが弱点だとわかる。センサーは「can also feel the first, weaker waves」とあり、観測所は「cost tens of thousands of dollars each」と高いのは観測所のほう。誤報の多さは批判として出たが「rarely happens by chance」と否定されている。

questions.question: According to the organizers, what is the main aim of repair cafés?
choices: To help residents save money on new products.
To teach people how to fix things by themselves.
To sell spare parts to the public at low prices.
To collect broken items so they can be recycled.
questions.explanation: 「the main goal is not simply to save money. Rather, they want visitors to watch and learn, so that next time they can make simple repairs on their own」と言っている。来場者が自分で修理できるようになることが目的で、正解はその言い換え。お金の節約は「not simply」で主な目的ではないと否定されている。交換部品を売らないのはメーカーの話で、リサイクルのために集めるという話はない。

questions.question: What is suggested about the laws the groups are asking for?
choices: They would allow the cafés to charge for repairs.
They would make the volunteers' work easier.
They would ban the use of glue in all products.
They have already been passed in Amsterdam.
questions.explanation: 製品が「glued shut or require special tools to open」で、メーカーが「refuse to sell spare parts」という問題を挙げ、「For this reason」と続けて、製品を「easier to repair」にする法律を求めていると言っている。法律ができればボランティアが修理しやすくなるということ。有料にする話はなく、接着剤を全面的に禁止するとも言っていない。アムステルダムは最初のリペアカフェが開かれた場所で、法律の話ではない。

questions.question: What happened after the British retailer introduced the fee?
choices: Its sales stayed about the same while its costs went down.
Many of its customers left for rival clothing stores.
It canceled the fee because of the early survey results.
Its competitors started offering free returns by mail.
questions.explanation: 専門家は客が競合店に移ると予想し、初期の調査も「seemed to support this」だったが、「However, the company's later figures showed that its sales had hardly changed, while the cost of handling returns fell sharply」と覆されている。最終的に有効なのは、売り上げはほぼ変わらず費用が減ったという結果。客が競合店に移ったというのは否定された予想。料金を取りやめたという話はなく、競合他社は「introduced similar fees」と同じく有料にした。

questions.question: Why do most of the retailers keep in-store returns free?
choices: Customers are less likely to order several sizes there.
Analysts warned that store sales would fall without it.
Returns by mail have become free again in Britain.
Shoppers who come in often buy other items as well.
questions.explanation: 「returns brought to a physical store remain free」の理由として「brings customers into their stores, where many end up buying something else」と言っている。店に来た客の多くがほかの物も買うからで、正解はその言い換え。複数のサイズを注文するのはネット通販で返品が増えた例で、店頭との比較はしていない。専門家が警告したのは客が競合店に移ることで、外れた予想。郵送の返品は有料にした話で、無料に戻ったとは言っていない。

questions.question: What did the hospital in the Netherlands do?
choices: It gave earplugs to the patients in every ward.
It stopped staff from talking in wards at night.
It changed the way staff are notified of alarms.
It shortened patients' stays to reduce the noise.
questions.explanation: 耳栓には「many patients find them uncomfortable」「patients will not hear when someone speaks to them」という問題があると述べた後、「A hospital in the Netherlands took a different approach」と続け、警報を「sent silently to nurses' handheld devices」ようにしたと言っている。警報を看護師に知らせる方法を変えたということで、正解はその言い換え。耳栓は別の病院が試し、問題があるとされた方法。職員の会話は騒音の原因として挙げられただけで、禁止したとは言っていない。入院期間が短くなったのは結果で、騒音を減らすための手段ではない。

questions.question: What do the researchers suggest about the results?
choices: The new system made hospital stays a little longer.
Another factor may also have helped patients sleep.
Patients slept better only when they wore earplugs.
The alarms had become louder after the renovation.
questions.explanation: 研究者は「the hospital also renovated its wards during the same period, so the improvement cannot be credited to the alarm system alone」と言っている。同じ時期の病棟の改装も睡眠の改善に関わった可能性があるということで、正解はその言い換え。入院期間は「became slightly shorter」で、長くなったのではない。耳栓はオランダの病院の方法ではない。改装の後に警報が大きくなったという話はない。

title: Cultivated meat and its climate claims

questions.question: Why did the researchers question the companies' claim?
choices: The steel tanks used for growing cells are costly to build.
News reports had changed the figure the companies gave.
Cleaning the cells' nutrient liquid uses a lot of power.
Beef farms have recently become much cleaner than before.
questions.explanation: 研究者は「the cells are grown in a nutrient liquid that must be highly purified, a process that uses large amounts of energy」と指摘している。細胞を育てる栄養液の精製に多くのエネルギーがかかることが理由で、正解はその言い換え。鋼鉄のタンクは作り方の説明に出るだけで、費用の話はない。報道は「repeated this figure」で、数字を変えたのではない。牛肉の生産がきれいになったという話はない。

questions.question: What do some of the companies now say about cultivated meat?
choices: It reduces emissions by more than ninety percent.
Its value for the climate relies on how it is produced.
It creates more emissions than ordinary beef does.
It is already cheaper to make than conventional beef.
questions.explanation: 企業は「withdrawing their original claim」の後、「the benefit depends on two conditions」として、再生可能エネルギーで工場を動かすことと、安い栄養分を開発することを挙げている。気候への利点は作り方しだいということで、正解はそのまとめた言い換え。90%以上減らすというのは取り下げられた当初の主張。牛肉より排出が多くなりうると言ったのは研究者で、しかも化石燃料を使う場合の話。「cheaper」は栄養分の条件として出るだけで、培養肉がもう安いとは言っていない。

questions.question: According to the 2014 study, why did students who wrote by hand do better?
choices: They copied more of the lecturer's exact words.
They were better at remembering simple facts.
They had to pick out key points and restate them.
They could record nearly the whole lecture.
questions.explanation: 「because handwriting is slow, students cannot copy every word」と「they are forced to decide what matters and put it into their own words, and this extra effort helps them learn」をつなぐと、手書きでは大事な点を選んで自分の言葉で言い直すしかなく、それが学習につながったとわかる。正解はその言い換え。講師の言葉をそのまま書き写すことは「cannot copy every word」で否定されている。研究で差が出たのは「understand ideas, rather than simply remember facts」で、事実の記憶ではない。講義をほとんど記録できるのはタイプする学生の利点として出た内容。

questions.question: What is suggested about many instructors today?
choices: They require all of their students to write their notes by hand.
They believe the 2014 study has now been fully confirmed.
They care more about how notes are taken than about the device.
They allow laptops only for students with certain disabilities.
questions.explanation: 「a growing number of instructors no longer ban laptops」と「they encourage students to type less and summarize more, whichever tool they use」をつなぐと、講師は道具そのものより、要約しながらノートを取るという取り方を重視しているとわかる。全員に手書きを求めるのは「no longer ban laptops」と合わない。その後の研究は「produced mixed results」で、完全に裏づけられたとは言っていない。障害のある学生の話はノートパソコンを禁止しない理由の1つで、その学生だけに認めるとは言っていない。

questions.question: What happened to the buildings that were repaired with cement?
choices: The stone stayed safe, just as experts had predicted.
The walls were able to dry out more quickly than before.
The material harmed the stone it was meant to protect.
The repairs were delayed for years by a lack of workers.
questions.explanation: 当時は「experts believed it would protect the old stone for centuries」と考えられていたが、「By the 1990s, however, it had become clear that cement traps moisture inside walls, causing the softer stone around it to crack and crumble」と覆されている。最終的に分かったのは、守るはずだった石をかえって傷めたということ。石が守られたというのは、後で誤りと分かった当時の予想。壁が自然に乾くのは石灰モルタルの性質で、セメントは湿気を閉じ込める。職人不足で工事が遅れたのは、石灰モルタルを義務づけた後の問題。

questions.question: How did the French agency deal with the shortage of skilled workers?
choices: It allowed restorers to use cement again for a while.
It postponed its restoration projects for several years.
It brought in experienced builders from other countries.
It paid for new workers to learn the traditional skills.
questions.explanation: 「Rather than relaxing the rule, one heritage agency in France decided to pay young builders to train alongside the last remaining experts」と言っている。若い職人にお金を払って昔ながらの技術を身につけさせたので、正解はその言い換え。セメントに戻すのは「Rather than relaxing the rule」で退けられた方法。何年も遅れたのは職人不足で起きた問題で、機関の対策ではない。ほかの国から職人を呼んだという話はない。

questions.question: What do recent studies suggest?
choices: High-rise offices lit overnight draw especially large numbers of birds.
Streetlights are the main reason birds lose their way at night.
Birds depend on the moon more than on the stars to navigate.
Weather radar interferes with birds' sense of the magnetic field.
questions.explanation: 「For many years, city officials assumed that streetlights were the main cause of the problem」の後に、「Yet recent studies using weather radar suggest that tall office towers, whose lights often stay on all night, attract far more birds」と続く。2つの文をつなぐと、以前の考えが改められ、夜通し明るい高層オフィスのほうが多くの鳥を引き寄せるとわかったことになる。街灯が主な原因というのは、否定された以前の考え。月の話は出てこない。気象レーダーは研究に使った道具で、磁場を乱すという話はない。

questions.question: Why have many business owners agreed to take part in the programs?
choices: City laws now require all of them to join.
Birds have broken windows in their buildings.
Officials promised them lower streetlight costs.
Turning off lights also cuts the power they use.
questions.explanation: 「Taking part is voluntary, but the programs have also been promoted as a way to save energy, and this has helped persuade many business owners to join」とある。エネルギーの節約にもなることが参加の決め手になっており、正解はその言い換え。参加は「voluntary」(任意)なので、法律で義務づけられたわけではない。窓に鳥がぶつかる話はあるが、それが経営者の参加の理由だとは言っていない。街灯の費用の話はない。

title: Reading scrolls that cannot be unrolled

questions.question: Why was the writing hard to see in the images at first?
choices: The scrolls had broken into many small pieces.
The scanner could only show the outer layer.
The ink had been removed by earlier scholars.
The ink looked very similar to the burned material.
questions.explanation: 「The ink had been made from soot, so in the images it looked almost the same as the burned papyrus around it」と言っている。すすのインクと焼けたパピルスが画像の中でほとんど区別できなかったことが理由で、正解はその言い換え。粉々に壊れたのは18世紀に学者が手で広げようとした巻物の話で、画像で文字が見えなかった理由ではない。スキャナーとソフトウェアは巻かれた層を分けて平らなページとして見せるので、外側しか写らないのではない。学者がインクを取り除いたという話はない。

questions.question: What is suggested about the new method?
choices: It avoids the damage caused by earlier attempts.
It was first tried in the eighteenth century.
It requires the scrolls to be laid out flat.
It works only on scrolls that were not burned.
questions.explanation: 18世紀には「scholars tried to unroll some of them by hand, but most broke into pieces」と、手で広げて巻物を壊してしまった。新しい方法については最後に「read the remaining scrolls without ever touching them」と言っている。2か所を合わせると、触れずに読むので昔のように巻物を壊さずに済むことがわかる。18世紀は手で広げようとした時代で、新しい方法ではない。平らにするのは画像の中でソフトウェアが行うことで、巻物そのものを広げるのではない。この方法は炭になった巻物を読むためのもの。

questions.question: What did later research reveal about the enzyme that was first discovered?
choices: It could clean up plastic in the sea within several weeks.
It worked well only when it was heated to a high temperature.
It was too slow and could not handle most ocean plastic.
It could break down every kind of plastic found in rivers.
questions.explanation: 初めは「a possible answer to the plastic pollution in the world's oceans」と報じられたが、「Further research, however, showed that the natural enzyme worked extremely slowly」「It also had no effect on most of the plastic found in the sea」と見直された。働きが遅く、海のプラスチックの大半には効かないとわかったので、正解はその2点をまとめた言い換え。数週間で海をきれいにできるというのは、薄い切れ端にさえ数週間かかるという内容を取り違えたもの。高温でしか働かないのは、後から設計された速い型の性質で、最初の酵素の話ではない。どんなプラスチックでも分解できるという内容は「no effect on most of the plastic」と合わない。

questions.question: Why are the enzymes now mainly seen as a tool for factories?
choices: The French company owns the rights to every version of them.
Factories can produce plastic from them more cheaply than from oil.
News reports warned that releasing them could harm sea life.
The improved versions need conditions that are not found in nature.
questions.explanation: 「these only work at around seventy degrees Celsius, so they cannot simply be released into rivers or oceans」と「For this reason, researchers now see the enzymes mainly as a tool for factories」をつなぐと、改良した酵素は高温でしか働かず、自然の中では使えないことが理由だとわかる。フランスの企業は工場を建てた例として出ただけで、権利の話はない。そのプラスチックは「still costs more than plastic made from oil」で、石油より安いのではない。報道は海の汚染を解決すると期待した内容で、海の生き物への害を警告してはいない。

questions.question: Why did progress in the United Kingdom slow down?
choices: Shoppers noticed that their favorite foods tasted different.
People began adding more salt to their meals at the table.
Firms were not obliged to join, and official pressure faded.
New laws made it harder for companies to change recipes.
questions.explanation: 「taking part in the program was never required」と「When the government turned its attention to other issues, progress slowed」をつなぐと、参加が義務ではなく、政府の関心が離れて圧力が弱まったことが理由だとわかる。正解はその2点をまとめた言い換え。味の変化は「people rarely notice small changes in taste」で、気づかれないように減らしていた。食卓の塩入れは、塩の大半の出どころではないと最初に否定された内容。法律で上限を定めたのは南アフリカなどほかの国で、イギリスの話ではない。

questions.question: What does the speaker suggest about countries such as South Africa?
choices: They doubted that voluntary efforts would be enough.
They copied the approach first used in the United Kingdom.
They wanted companies to cut salt all at once.
They found that people noticed small changes in taste.
questions.explanation: イギリスでは参加が義務ではなく、進み方が鈍って塩分が増えた製品もあった。それを受けて「Partly because of this experience, several countries, including South Africa, have since passed laws ... rather than depending on companies to act on their own」と言っている。企業の自主的な取り組みだけでは足りないと考えて法律にしたとわかる。イギリスのやり方は任意の取り組みで、それをまねたのではなく法律に変えた。一度に減らすという話は出ていない。味のわずかな変化に気づかないというのはイギリスの企業が頼った研究の内容で、それを覆したという話はない。

title: Supermarket prices that change by the hour

questions.question: Why did the supermarket chain give up its original plan?
choices: The new labels could not change prices quickly enough.
Customers felt it was unfair to people who shop after work.
It did not succeed in spreading out customers' visits.
Economists warned that it would lower the store's profits.
questions.explanation: 当初の計画は混雑時に値段を上げるものだったが、「shoppers reacted angrily, saying that people with regular office hours would be punished simply for shopping after work」の後に「Within a month, the chain dropped the plan」と続く。仕事帰りに買う人に不公平だという客の反発で取りやめたので正解。値札は「within seconds」で値段を変えられる。来店を分散させる効果は会社の主張で、試した結果は述べていない。利益が減るという経済学者の警告は、取りやめた後の今の値下げのやり方についてのもの。

questions.question: What concern do some economists have about the chain's current approach?
choices: Prices may go up again during the busiest hours.
Fresh food may be thrown away more often than before.
Shoppers may wait for lower prices before buying.
Staff may have to change the price tags by hand.
questions.explanation: 今のやり方は「uses the labels only to cut prices」で、経済学者は「customers may learn to put off their shopping until the discounts begin」と警告している。値引きを待って買い物を遅らせるおそれなので正解。混雑時の値上げは取りやめた計画で、今のやり方ではない。食品の廃棄は「far less food than before」と減っている。値札は電子表示で中央のコンピューターから変えるので、手で替える話はない。

questions.question: According to some experts, why does homework do little for young children?
choices: They already remember what they learned in class.
They still lack the ability to study independently.
They are given much less of it than older students.
They usually find it too easy to hold their interest.
questions.explanation: 「homework has little effect on test scores」の理由として、専門家は「young children do not yet have the skills to study on their own」と説明し、そのため宿題の時間は「frustrating rather than useful」になると言っている。自分だけで勉強する力がまだ足りないのが理由で、正解はその言い換え。授業の内容を覚えるのに役立つというのは親が信じていることで、研究では小学生への効果は小さいとされている。年長の生徒と比べているのは宿題の効果で、量ではない。易しすぎて退屈だという話はなく、むしろいら立つと言っている。

questions.question: What concern do critics have about the reading policy?
choices: Reading every evening may put too much stress on pupils.
Twenty minutes a day may be too little to build vocabulary.
Pupils with less support at home may fall behind others.
Parents may complain that their children have no real homework.
questions.explanation: 批判する人は「the change may widen gaps between students」と心配し、その理由として「Children whose parents work late or cannot help them ... may end up reading far less than their classmates」と言っている。2か所をつなぐと、家で親の手助けを受けにくい子どもがほかの子どもに後れを取るおそれがあるという心配だとわかる。ストレスについては、支持する人が「without adding stress」と言っており、ストレスが増えるとは言っていない。語彙が増えるというのも支持する人の意見で、20分では足りないという話はない。親が宿題のないことに文句を言うという話は出てこない。

title: Museums and the return of cultural objects

questions.question: Why has the museums' traditional position become harder to defend?
choices: Most of the items turned out to have been bought legally.
Large international collections now attract fewer visitors.
Countries of origin can now look after the items properly.
Museums can no longer afford to keep the items safe.
questions.explanation: 博物館は返還を断る理由として「the objects were safer in their care」と主張していた。しかし「this position has become harder to defend」の理由として「Many countries of origin have now built modern museums of their own」と言っている。2か所をつなぐと、元の国でも品々をきちんと管理できるようになり、安全だという主張が成り立ちにくくなったとわかる。研究で明らかになったのは「some items were obtained by force」で、合法的に買ったのではない。国際的なコレクションの来館者が減ったという話はない。博物館が管理の費用を払えなくなったという話もない。

questions.question: What is true about the bronze sculptures now?
choices: Some are on show in Europe as works lent by their owner.
They are on loan to their country but owned by the museum.
All of them are now displayed only in their home country.
They still belong to the museum despite the critics.
questions.explanation: 博物館は2018年に、所有権を持ったまま貸し出す案を出したが、批判を受けて「the museum dropped the idea of a loan and handed over full ownership」と方針を変えた。さらにその国が「asked the museum to continue displaying several of them, this time as borrowed works」と頼んでいる。今は所有者である元の国から借りる形で、いくつかがヨーロッパの博物館に展示されている。所有権を持ったまま貸し出すのは取り下げられた案。すべてが元の国だけで展示されているのは、いくつかを博物館が展示し続けるという内容と合わない。博物館が所有権を持ち続けているのは、「handed over full ownership」と合わない。

questions.question: What is one reason owners give for ending tipping?
choices: Servers can earn more from each customer.
Kitchen workers can also receive better pay.
Customers can pay lower prices for meals.
Diners can judge the quality of service.
questions.explanation: オーナーたちは「it allows them to share money more fairly」と言い、続けて「Cooks and dishwashers traditionally receive no tips, but under the new system, they can be paid higher wages as well」と説明している。2文をつなぐと、厨房で働く人にも高い賃金を払えることが理由だとわかる。給仕係はむしろ「had often earned more under the old system」で、古い仕組みのほうが稼げた。メニューの価格は「raised」で、安くなっていない。チップは「depend more on a server's appearance than on the quality of the service」と言われており、客がサービスの質を判断できるという話ではない。

questions.question: Why did some restaurants go back to tipping?
choices: They lost skilled staff and seemed too costly to diners.
Their cooks felt that the new wages were still unfair.
Customers disliked paying tips on top of higher prices.
Research showed that the change hurt service quality.
questions.explanation: チップ制に戻った理由として、まず「Their most experienced servers ... left for restaurants where tips were still allowed」、次に「customers comparing menus online often assumed these restaurants were simply more expensive」と2つ述べている。経験のある従業員が辞め、客には高すぎる店に見えたので正解。調理師は賃金が上がった側で、不満を持ったという話はない。新しい仕組みではサービス料が価格に含まれ、チップは払わない。研究の話はチップが外見に左右されるというもので、サービスの質が下がったという内容ではない。

title: Listening for leaks in old water pipes

questions.question: Why did crews search for leaks late at night?
choices: Leaks made a louder hissing sound after dark.
The streets were quieter because there were fewer cars.
Less drinking water was being used in homes.
Water was more likely to come up through the road.
questions.explanation: 作業員が夜遅くに歩いた理由として「because that was when traffic noise was lowest」と言っている。車の騒音が一番小さい時間だったということで、正解はその言い換え。シューという音は、今のセンサーとコンピューターが聞き分ける音として出てきただけで、夜に大きくなるとは言っていない。家庭で使う水の量が夜に減るという話はない。道路から水が出てくるのは、センサーが知らせるより何週間も後のことで、夜とは関係がない。

questions.question: What does the speaker suggest about the new technology?
choices: It cannot find a leak until water reaches the surface.
Metal pipes carry sound too far for the sensors to work well.
The computers often mistake traffic noise for leaking water.
Cities that have updated their pipes may find it more expensive.
questions.explanation: プラスチックの管は「carry sound over much shorter distances than metal ones」ので、「far more sensors are needed, which raises costs for cities that have already replaced many of their old pipes with plastic」と言っている。古い管をすでに新しい管に替えた都市ほど、この技術の費用が高くなるということで、正解はその言い換え。センサーは「often weeks before any water comes up through the road」に知らせるので、水が出てくるまで見つけられないのではない。音を遠くまで伝えるのは金属の管の長所として出てきた。車の騒音は昔の作業の話で、コンピューターが聞き間違えるとは言っていない。

questions.question: What is one benefit of green roofs?
choices: They produce fresh vegetables for local residents.
They raise the price of nearby houses.
They reduce the energy needed to cool buildings.
They provide safe homes for city birds.
questions.explanation: 「Plants on the roof keep the building cooler, so people inside use less electricity for air conditioning」と述べられている。建物を冷やすための電気が少なくて済む。野菜が採れる、近くの家の値段が上がる、鳥のすみかになる、は本文にない。

questions.question: What are some city governments doing?
choices: Offering funds to owners who add green roofs.
Banning the construction of new buildings.
Asking residents to paint their roofs white.
Building new parks on empty land.
questions.explanation: 最後に「some city governments now give money to building owners who want to add one」と述べられている。屋上緑化をする建物の所有者にお金を出している。新しい建物の禁止、屋根を白く塗る呼びかけ、空き地への公園づくりは本文にない。

title: Taking the stairs instead of the elevator

questions.question: What did the study find about the office workers?
choices: Their legs grew more powerful.
They preferred the elevator after twelve weeks.
They had trouble breathing on the stairs.
They walked up fewer floors each week.
questions.explanation: 「the muscles in their legs had become stronger」とある。脚の力が強くなった(more powerful)。12週間後にエレベーターを好むようになったという話はない。息については「without getting out of breath」で、息が苦しくなったのではない。上る階数が減ったという話もない。

questions.question: What do doctors advise some people to do?
choices: Get medical advice and start with a small amount.
Listen to music while they climb the stairs.
Avoid using the stairs for the first twelve weeks.
Take the elevator if they work on a high floor.
questions.explanation: 「people with knee or heart problems should talk to a doctor first and begin with just one or two floors」とある。まず医師に相談し、少しの量から始める。階段で音楽を流すのは会社の取り組みで、医師の助言ではない。12週間は研究の期間。高い階で働く人へのエレベーターの話はない。

questions.question: What did one study find about children who had taken music lessons for two years?
choices: They learned to read music more quickly.
They were more easily distracted by sounds.
They also did better in art classes.
They did better on tests of short-term memory.
questions.explanation: 「children who had taken music lessons for two years scored higher on memory tasks than children who had not」とある。ここでの記憶はワーキングメモリー、つまり「the ability to hold information in mind for a short time」のことなので、短い間覚えておく力の課題で成績がよかったという言い換えが正解。楽譜を読むのは楽器を弾くときに必要なこととして出てくるだけで、速く読めるようになったという話はない。音については「better at concentrating, especially when they had to ignore distracting sounds」で、気が散りやすくなったのではなく逆。美術の教室は後の実験で比べた相手で、そこで成績がよかったという話はない。

questions.question: What do other researchers suggest about the results of the first study?
choices: Advantages at home may partly explain them.
Art classes may train memory even better.
Two years of lessons may be too short a time.
Children who practice alone may remember more.
questions.explanation: 別の研究者は「families who pay for lessons often have more time and money to support their children's education in other ways」と指摘している。レッスンを受けた子どもの成績がよかったのは、音楽そのものより家庭の恵まれた環境のためかもしれないということで、正解はその言い換え。美術の教室との比較では「the differences between the two groups turned out to be small」で、美術のほうが効果が大きいとは言っていない。2年間が短すぎるという話も、1人で練習する子どもの話も出てこない。

questions.question: What is one advantage of 3D-printed houses?
choices: Their roofs can also be finished in two days.
They can be built without any workers on site.
They are easier to inspect than wooden homes.
They leave almost no unused building material.
questions.explanation: 利点として「very little material is wasted because the machine uses only the amount the design requires」と言っている。材料がほとんど余らないということで、正解はその言い換え。2日で完成するのは「The walls of a small house」で、屋根は「workers must still install roofs … by hand」と手で取り付ける。作業員がいらないわけではない。検査については「officials are often unsure how to inspect printed walls」と、むしろ難しい。

questions.question: Why have some projects been delayed?
choices: The printers broke down while building the walls.
Charities could not raise enough money in time.
Workers needed several months to print the walls.
Officials lack clear standards for checking the walls.
questions.explanation: 「building rules in many areas were written for traditional materials … so officials are often unsure how to inspect printed walls」と言い、「As a result, some projects have had to wait months for approval」と続けている。規則が従来の材料向けで、印刷された壁を検査する基準がはっきりしないことが遅れの理由。プリンターが故障したという話はない。慈善団体は災害後に家を用意した例として出てくるだけで、資金不足の話はない。印刷は「the printing itself took only days」と数日で終わっている。

questions.question: Why did employees at the firm take less time off under the new policy?
choices: Their workloads grew after the policy began.
They feared seeming less dedicated than others.
Their managers told them to avoid long breaks.
The policy allowed them only fifteen days a year.
questions.explanation: 「many employees were unsure how much leave was acceptable, and they worried that taking time off would make them look less committed than their coworkers」と言っている。休むと同僚より熱意がないように見えると恐れたことが理由で、正解はその言い換え。仕事量が増えたという話はない。管理職は「tried encouraging staff to take more breaks」と、むしろ休むよう勧めている。15日は後から加えた「at least fifteen days」という最低日数で、上限ではなく、休みが減った時期の制度でもない。

questions.question: What is true about the firm's vacation policy now?
choices: Staff are once again given a fixed number of vacation days.
Managers simply encourage staff to take more time off.
Employees may take no more than fifteen days off a year.
Staff can take any amount of leave above a required minimum.
questions.explanation: 会社は「kept unlimited leave and added a rule requiring every employee to take at least fifteen days off each year」とした。無制限の休暇は残り、最低15日は休まなければならないので、最低日数を超えればいくらでも休める。休暇の日数を決める制度に戻す案は「the company rejected the idea」と退けられた。休むよう勧めるだけのやり方は「this had little effect」で、その後に規則が加えられた。15日は「at least」で最低日数であり、上限ではない。

questions.question: What do some young photographers say about using film?
choices: It gives better image quality than their smartphones.
It costs less than buying a new digital camera does.
Its limits make them more thoughtful about each picture.
They like being able to check each photo right away.
