questions.explanation: 若い写真家の一部は「because each roll allows only a limited number of shots, they think more carefully before pressing the button」と言っている。撮れる枚数が限られていることで、1枚ずつよく考えて撮るようになるということで、正解はその言い換え。画質がスマートフォンより良いという話はない。費用については、古いカメラの価格が「risen sharply」と上がった話しかない。すぐに確認できるのとは逆で、「not knowing how their pictures will turn out until they are developed」を楽しむ人もいると言っている。

questions.question: Why have some camera shops started training courses?
choices: Young customers want to learn how to develop their own film.
Fewer people are now able to keep old cameras in working order.
Manufacturers have asked them to help design new film cameras.
Prices of used cameras have become too high for them to sell.
questions.explanation: 「Many of the technicians who understood their mechanical parts have retired, and spare parts are no longer made」と述べたあと、「To deal with this」と続けて研修の話をしている。2か所をつなぐと、古いカメラを直せる人が減っているのが理由だと分かる。研修で教えるのは「how to fix old cameras」で、現像の仕方ではなく、対象も客ではなく若い店員。メーカーは新しいカメラをほとんど作っておらず、設計を頼んだという話もない。中古の価格が上がったことは問題として挙げられているが、研修の理由ではない。

questions.question: Why do peat bogs hold so much carbon?
choices: Constant wetness stops dead plants from fully decaying.
They cover a larger share of land than the world's forests.
Farmers have added dead plants to the soil for centuries.
The smoke from burning peat is trapped under the ground.
questions.explanation: 「Because the ground is always wet, the plants never fully break down, and the carbon they contain stays locked in the soil」とある。地面が常に湿っているので植物が分解しきらず、炭素が土に残るということで、正解はその言い換え。湿原は「only about three percent of the world's land」で、森林より広いわけではない(炭素の量が森林より多い)。農業は湿原の水を抜いた理由として出てくるだけ。泥炭を燃やすと炭素は空気中に出ていく。

questions.question: What do scientists say about restored bogs?
choices: They are now more valuable than the remaining bogs.
Plants that need wet ground have failed to return.
New drainage ditches are needed to protect them.
Their benefits for the climate will appear only slowly.
questions.explanation: 科学者は「restored bogs may take decades to start storing large amounts of carbon again」と警告している。再生した湿原が炭素を蓄えて気候に役立つまでには時間がかかるということで、正解はその言い換え。最も重要なのは「protecting the bogs that remain」で、再生した湿原のほうが価値が高いとは言っていない。湿った土地の植物は「are returning」と戻ってきている。排水溝は再生のためにふさいでいるもので、新しく掘る話ではない。

questions.question: According to the speaker, how can beaver dams benefit people?
choices: By lowering the chance of floods in some towns.
By supplying wood for local building projects.
By keeping farmers' fields dry during heavy rain.
By making river water flow more quickly.
questions.explanation: 「During heavy rain, these ponds hold back large amounts of water, so towns further downstream are less likely to flood」とある。下流の町で洪水が起きにくくなるということで、正解はその言い換え。ダムは枝と泥で作られるが、木材を人に提供する話はない。畑については「caused water to cover their fields」と、むしろ水に覆われると農家が言っている。ダムは「slow down the flow of water」で、流れを速くするのではない。

questions.question: What is one thing the government has done?
choices: It banned farmers from removing any beaver dams.
It released beavers only into rivers far from farms.
It paid hunters to reduce the number of beavers.
It offered money to farmers who keep riverside land wet.
questions.explanation: 「It has also started paying farmers who agree to leave wet areas along rivers for wildlife」とある。川沿いの湿った土地を残す農家にお金を払っているということで、正解はその言い換え。ダムは「allows dams to be removed in certain places, but only with official permission」で、取り除くことが全面的に禁止されているわけではない。農場から遠い川だけに放したという話はない。狩猟はビーバーが姿を消した昔の原因で、政府が今お金を払っているわけではない。

title: Letting residents vote on city spending

questions.question: According to the speaker, what is one benefit of participatory budgeting?
choices: Cities can spend less money on new playgrounds.
Residents take a more active part in local affairs.
Elected officials have more time for other work.
Street lights can be installed more quickly.
questions.explanation: 支持する人々は「this makes people feel more connected to their local government」と言い、「the number of people attending neighborhood meetings doubled」という例も挙げている。住民が地元の行政により積極的に関わるようになるということで、正解はその言い換え。遊び場(playgrounds)や街灯(street lights)は住民が提案する事業の例で、費用が減る・早く付くという話ではない。公職者の時間が増えるという話はない。

questions.question: What have some cities done to deal with a problem?
choices: Made voting more convenient for people with less free time.
Allowed only retirees to vote on the city budget.
Asked working parents to attend more neighborhood meetings.
Stopped holding budget meetings at local schools.
questions.explanation: 問題は、投票するのが時間のある人に偏り「the needs of busy working parents may be overlooked」こと。その対応として「allow residents to vote online and have set up voting booths at schools and supermarkets」とある。時間の少ない人でも投票しやすくしたということで、正解はその言い換え。退職者(retirees)だけに投票させるのは逆の内容。働く親に集会への参加を求めたという話はない。学校には投票所を設けたのであって、集会をやめたのではない。

questions.question: Why did the instrument-lending programs begin?
choices: Libraries had too many books on their shelves.
Buying an instrument is too expensive for many families.
Music teachers needed more space for their classes.
Children were borrowing fewer novels than before.
questions.explanation: 「These programs began because many families cannot afford to buy an instrument」とある。楽器を買う余裕がない家庭が多いということで、cannot afford を too expensive と言い換えたものが正解。本(books)が多すぎるという話はない。教師が場所を必要としていたという話はない。小説(novel)は借り方のたとえで、子どもが借りなくなったという話はない。

questions.question: What do some local music teachers do for the libraries?
choices: They lend their own guitars to members.
They manage the waiting lists for instruments.
They teach free classes inside the libraries.
They inspect the instruments regularly.
questions.explanation: 「a few libraries have asked local music teachers to check the instruments regularly」とある。楽器を定期的に点検するということで、check を inspect と言い換えたものが正解。ギター(guitars)は図書館が貸すもので、教師が自分の楽器を貸すのではない。待っている人の名簿を管理する話はない。教師は掲示板でレッスンを宣伝できるが、無料で教えるという話はない。

title: The return of night trains in Europe

questions.question: Why have night trains become popular again?
choices: Flights within Europe have become more expensive.
They are seen as a cleaner way to travel.
Many hotels near train stations have closed.
Sleeping cars can now carry more passengers.
questions.explanation: 「many travelers are concerned about the environment, and a train journey produces far less carbon dioxide than a flight」とある。環境への負担が少ない移動手段と見られているということで、正解はその言い換え。格安の航空便(flights)は夜行列車が減った原因で、高くなったという話はない。ホテル(hotel)は代金を浮かせられるという話で、閉まったのではない。寝台車は「carry fewer passengers」で、逆の内容。

questions.question: What is one difficulty of running night trains?
choices: Passengers do not like sleeping on board.
Governments have banned new international routes.
Most stations are closed during the night.
Fares have to be set relatively high.
questions.explanation: 「Sleeping cars carry fewer passengers than ordinary seats, so tickets must be fairly expensive to cover the costs」とある。運賃をある程度高くしなければならないということで、正解はその言い換え。乗客は車内で眠ることを好んでいる(on board は本文の語)。政府は路線を禁止したのではなく、費用の分担に合意した。駅が夜に閉まるという話はない。

title: Solar panels that float on reservoirs

questions.question: What is one advantage of floating solar panels?
choices: They help prevent water from being lost.
They make it possible to grow food on lakes.
They work best when the weather is cold.
They cost less to build than panels on land.
questions.explanation: パネルは水に日陰を作り、「which reduces the amount of water that evaporates in summer」と述べている。水が蒸発して失われるのを防ぐということで、正解はその言い換え。食料(food)は畑が必要な理由として出てくるだけで、湖で食料を育てる話ではない。効率がよいのは寒い時期ではなく「during hot weather」。建設費の話はない。

questions.question: What have some governments done?
choices: Banned solar panels from lakes that have fish.
Asked scientists to grow more water plants.
Limited how much of a reservoir the panels can cover.
Required companies to build panels on farmland.
questions.explanation: 一部の政府は「allow floating panels to cover only a certain share of a reservoir's surface」としている。貯水池のどれだけを覆ってよいかを制限したということで、正解はその言い換え。魚(fish)のいる湖での禁止ではなく、割合の制限。科学者は野生生物への影響を調べているだけで、水草を増やすよう頼まれてはいない。畑(farmland)に作らせるという話はない。

title: Tall buildings made of engineered wood

questions.question: According to supporters, why are wooden buildings good for the environment?
choices: They need less wood than older buildings did.
They can easily be taken apart and reused.
They lead to fewer trees being cut down.
They hold carbon for a long period of time.
questions.explanation: 支持する人たちは、木は育つときに炭素を吸収し、「this carbon remains locked inside the wood for as long as the building stands」と言っている。建物がある限り炭素を長く閉じ込めておけるということで、正解はその言い換え。使う木材の量が少ないという話はない。解体して再利用する話もない。伐採については、批判する人たちが森の伐採が速すぎれば害になると言っており、伐採が減るとは言っていない。

questions.question: Why have several cities changed their building rules?
choices: Forests are now growing faster than before.
Concrete buildings were found to burn easily.
Tests reduced worries about the risk of fire.
Critics called for stricter limits on height.
questions.explanation: 「Fire safety was also a concern at first」と述べたあと、試験で厚い木材は炭の層が内側を守ると分かったと言い、「As a result」と続けて規則の変更を述べている。2か所をつなぐと、試験で火災への心配が小さくなったことが理由だと分かる。森が前より速く育っているという話はなく、伐採が速すぎることが心配されている。コンクリートの建物が燃えやすいという話はない。批判する人たちが高さの制限を求めたという話もなく、規則はより高い建物を認める方向に変わった。

questions.question: Why do many of the robots work at night?
choices: There are fewer workers on the farm.
The fruit is harder at that time.
Their cameras work better in the dark.
Electricity costs less at night.
questions.explanation: 「Many of them work at night, when the fruit is cool and firm」と述べている。夜は実が硬いので、正解はその言い換え。働き手の少なさは収穫期の問題として出てくるが、夜に働く理由ではない。カメラ(cameras)は実を見つけるために使うもので、暗いほうがよく見えるとは言っていない。電気代の話はない。

questions.question: What have some companies started doing?
choices: Offering robots to farms for a limited period.
Selling cheaper robots to small farms.
Training farm workers to use robots.
Building robots with faster arms.
questions.explanation: 「some companies now rent the robots to farmers only during the harvest season」と述べている。収穫期の間だけロボットを貸すということで、正解はその言い換え。安いロボットを売るのではなく、貸すことで手が届きやすくしている。働き手の研修の話はない。アーム(arms)は柔らかいと言っているだけで、速いアームを作る話はない。

title: Teaching children to manage money at school

questions.question: According to supporters, what is one benefit of these lessons?
choices: Students can earn money by running their own shops.
Children may get higher scores on math tests.
People may avoid owing large amounts later in life.
Families may spend less money on things they want.
questions.explanation: 支持する人たちは「adults who learned these skills as children are less likely to fall into serious debt」と言っている。大人になって大きな借金を抱えにくいということで、正解はその言い換え。店(shop)の運営は本物のお金を扱う練習で、稼ぐためではない。算数のテストの話はない。欲しいもの(wants)は授業で学ぶ区別として出てくるだけで、家族の支出が減るという話はない。

questions.question: Why do some programs send activities home?
choices: Parents strongly affect children's attitudes toward money.
Schools do not have enough class time for the lessons.
Children want to practice running shops at home.
Teachers need parents to check students' budgets.
questions.explanation: 「what parents say and do about money influences children more than classroom lessons do」と述べ、「For this reason」と続けて家庭に課題を送る話をしている。親の影響が大きいことが理由で、正解はその言い換え。授業時間が足りないという話はない。店の運営は学校で行うもの。教師が親に予算を確認してほしいという話はない。

questions.question: Why did output at many companies stay about the same?
choices: Companies hired extra staff to cover the missing day.
Workers used their time more efficiently.
Employees worked longer hours on the other days.
Workers were paid more for doing the same work.
questions.explanation: 生産量が変わらなかった理由は「as employees spent less time in unnecessary meetings and focused more on important tasks」と述べている。不要な会議を減らし重要な仕事に集中したことをまとめると、時間を効率よく使ったということになる。追加の人を雇うのは病院や店で起きることで、生産量が変わらなかった理由ではない。ほかの日に長く働いたという話はない。給料は「the same pay」で、増えていない。

questions.question: What concern do some economists have?
choices: The trial results may not apply to all companies.
Shorter weeks may make workers more tired.
Governments are spending too much on research.
Hospitals have refused to take part in the trials.
questions.explanation: 一部の経済学者は、試験に手を挙げた企業は「may have been ones that already expected the system to work well」と指摘し、さらに研究が必要だと言っている。参加した企業が偏っていたかもしれないので、結果がすべての企業に当てはまるとは限らないという懸念だと考えられる。疲れは「less tired」と減ったと報告されている。政府の研究費の話はない。病院は費用が上がる例として出てくるだけで、参加を断ったとは言っていない。

title: The changing story of an old stone bridge

questions.question: What did the scientists find?
choices: The bridge was built entirely in the twelfth century.
The Romans repaired the bridge after a flood.
The records found in the 1990s were not genuine.
Both earlier views of the bridge were partly correct.
questions.explanation: 住民はローマ時代の橋だと信じ、1990年代の記録は12世紀に造られたとしていた。科学者は「the lowest part of the bridge is indeed Roman, while the upper sections were rebuilt in the twelfth century」と突き止めた。どちらの見方も一部は正しかったということで、正解はそれをまとめた言い換え。すべてが12世紀に造られたというのは1990年代の説で、くつがえされた。洪水の後に造り直したのはローマ人ではなく12世紀の人々。記録が偽物だったという話はない。

questions.question: How does the town now present the bridge?
choices: As a monument built entirely by the Romans.
As a bridge that dates from the twelfth century.
As a structure whose age is still unknown.
As having been made at two different times.
questions.explanation: 「the town now describes the bridge as a structure built in two periods」と述べている。2つの時代に造られたものとして紹介しているので、正解はその言い換え。ローマ時代の遺跡というのは昔の説明。12世紀の橋というのは1990年代以降のガイドブックの説明で、今は1つの年代を選んでいない。年代がまだ分からないという話ではなく、2つの時代と分かっている。

title: Seaweed farms and cleaner coastal water

questions.question: How does seaweed help coastal water?
choices: It adds oxygen to the water at night.
It keeps fish away from the coast.
It removes some extra nutrients.
It stops algae from growing in winter.
questions.explanation: 「As seaweed grows, it takes in some of the extra nutrients from the water」と述べている。余分な栄養分を取り除くので、正解はその言い換え。酸素(oxygen)は藻が増えすぎると減るもので、海藻が夜に増やすとは言っていない。魚を遠ざける、冬に藻を止める、という話はない。

questions.question: What do scientists say?
choices: Seaweed should not be sold as food.
Cutting waste from land matters most.
Seaweed farms create too few jobs.
Fertilizer made from seaweed is unsafe.
questions.explanation: 科学者は「the most important step is still to reduce the amount of waste that enters the sea from land」と言っている。陸からの排水を減らすことが最も大事なので、正解はその言い換え。海藻は食品として売れると述べている。仕事(jobs)は生み出すと言っており、少なすぎるとは言っていない。海藻から作る肥料が危ないという話はない。

title: Slowing ships down to protect whales

questions.question: Why is underwater noise a problem for whales?
choices: It makes it harder for them to send signals.
It causes them to swim into busy ports.
It prevents ships from noticing them.
It drives the fish they eat to deeper water.
questions.explanation: 「Whales depend on sound to find food and to communicate with each other, so this noise can make it harder for them to survive」と述べている。騒音のせいで仲間と意思を伝え合いにくくなるので、正解はその言い換え。港(ports)は船に速度を落とすよう求めている側で、クジラが港に迷い込むのではない。船がクジラに気づかない、餌の魚が深く逃げる、という話はない。

questions.question: What have several ports done?
choices: Charged ships extra for using more fuel.
Banned large ships from busy lanes.
Rewarded ships that join the program.
Paid researchers to count whale deaths.
questions.explanation: 「Several ports now offer lower fees to ships that take part」と述べている。参加する船の料金を下げて報いているので、正解はその言い換え。燃料(fuel)は速度を落とすと減ったという話で、多く使う船に追加料金を取るのではない。大型船を航路から締め出す話はない。クジラの死亡を調べたのは研究者で、港がお金を払ったとは言っていない。

title: Praising children's effort instead of intelligence

questions.question: Why do some children avoid difficult tasks?
choices: They worry failing would change others' opinion of them.
They have been told that the tasks are not useful.
They are praised only for the effort they make.
They have not been taught any useful strategies.
questions.explanation: 頭がいいとほめられた子どもは難しい課題を避け、その理由は「failing might show that they are not as smart as people think」と述べている。失敗すると周りの評価が変わるのを心配しているということで、正解はそれをまとめた言い換え。課題が役に立たないと言われた話はない。努力をほめられた子どもはむしろ難しい問題を選ぶ。方法(strategies)を教わっていないという話はない。

questions.question: What do some researchers suggest?
choices: Adults should stop praising children's effort.
Children should hear that they are clever more often.
Children should be given easier problems at first.
Praise should come with advice about new approaches.
questions.explanation: 研究者は、進歩がないときに「good effort」と言うだけでは役に立たないとし、「adults should also discuss with children what they could try differently next time」と提案している。ほめるだけでなく、次の試し方の助言も添えるということで、正解はその言い換え。努力をほめるのをやめるのではなく、それだけでは足りないという話。頭がいいとほめるのは逆効果とされた方法。易しい問題から始めるという話はない。

questions.question: What happened to the salary ranges in the city?
choices: Most became narrower after the city took action.
They remained too wide to give useful information.
They were removed from most job advertisements.
They grew wider after the study was published.
questions.explanation: 最初は幅の広いものもあったが、「after the city began publishing examples of unclear ads, most companies narrowed them」と述べている。市が対策をとった後にほとんどが狭まったので、正解はその言い換え。役に立たないほど広いままというのは批判者の予想で、「only partly correct」とされた。広告から消えた、調査の後に広がった、という話はない。

questions.question: What did the researchers see as the main benefit of the rule?
choices: The pay gap between men and women closed.
New employees received much higher salaries.
Applicants became better at negotiating pay.
Companies were able to fill jobs more quickly.
questions.explanation: 研究者は「the main benefit was not higher pay but shorter hiring processes」と結論づけている。採用が早く済むようになったのが主な利点で、正解はその言い換え。男女の賃金格差の縮小は支持者が期待したことで、結果としては述べていない。提示額は「rose slightly」で、大きく上がったのではなく、主な利点とも否定されている。交渉がうまくなったという話はない。

title: Walking in forests to reduce stress

questions.question: What is forest bathing?
choices: Swimming in a cold mountain lake
Walking slowly through a forest
Planting flowers in a garden
Sleeping outside in a tent
questions.explanation: 「It simply means walking slowly through a forest and paying attention to the sights, sounds, and smells around you」と述べている。森の中をゆっくり歩くことなので正解。山の湖で泳ぐ、庭に花を植える、テントで寝る、という話はない。

questions.question: Why do researchers say more studies are needed?
choices: Most experiments so far have been small.
The tests cost too much money.
Some patients felt sick afterward.
Many people refused to take part.
questions.explanation: 「more studies are needed, because most experiments so far have been small」と述べている。これまでの実験のほとんどが小規模だったので正解。費用がかかりすぎた、気分が悪くなった患者がいた、参加を断った人が多かった、という話はない。

title: Concrete that repairs its own cracks

questions.question: Why does ordinary concrete need regular repairs?
choices: Water entering cracks harms the metal inside.
Bacteria slowly break down the limestone in it.
The steel inside makes it crack in cold weather.
Bridges and tunnels now carry heavier loads.
questions.explanation: 「Water gets into these cracks and damages the steel inside, so bridges and tunnels need regular and expensive repairs」と述べている。ひびから入った水が中の鉄を傷めるので、正解はその言い換え。細菌は新しいコンクリートで石灰石を作る側で、壊すのではない。鉄筋がひびの原因、橋やトンネルにかかる重さが増えた、という話はない。

questions.question: What do engineers say about the new concrete?
choices: It is already cheaper to produce than ordinary concrete.
Its higher price could be balanced by lower repair costs.
It can seal cracks of any width within a few weeks.
It should be used only for tunnels and bridges.
questions.explanation: 「The material currently costs more than ordinary concrete, but engineers argue that it could save money over the life of a structure, because fewer repairs would be needed」と述べている。高い分を補修費の少なさで取り戻せるので、正解はその言い換え。今は普通のコンクリートより高い。ふさがるのは「up to about one millimeter wide」のひびで、どんな幅でもではない。トンネルと橋だけに使うべきだとは言っていない。

title: Smaller packages at the same price

questions.question: Why do many companies make their products smaller?
choices: They fear losing customers to lower-priced brands.
Smaller packages cost less to transport.
Governments have banned large price increases.
Shoppers have asked for smaller portions.
questions.explanation: 「Raising prices can drive customers to cheaper brands, so many companies instead reduce the size of their products」と述べている。値上げで客を安いブランドに取られるのを恐れているので、正解はその言い換え。輸送費、値上げの禁止、客が少ない量を望んだ、という話はない(政府の対応は量を減らした後の話)。

questions.question: What is one result of the rule in France?
choices: Manufacturers have redesigned their packaging.
The prices of most foods have gone down.
Some stores have stopped selling certain products.
Supermarkets now decide the size of products.
questions.explanation: 小売業者は規則に不満を持ち、「some have started removing brands that shrink their products from their shelves rather than displaying the warnings」と述べている。製品を小さくしたブランドを棚から外す店が出てきた、つまり一部の商品を売らなくなったので、正解はその言い換え。包装を変えた、多くの食品が値下がりした、という話はない。小売業者は「decisions made by manufacturers」の責任を負わされると不満を述べており、大きさを決めるのはメーカーのまま。

questions.question: What did later research find about players' improvements?
choices: They were mostly limited to the games themselves.
They prevented memory loss in older adults.
They helped players remember shopping lists.
They continued for about fifteen years.
questions.explanation: 初期の研究では「players quickly became much better at the games」とされたが、その後の研究で「these improvements rarely carried over to other tasks」と分かった。上達はほとんどゲームの中だけだったので、正解はその言い換え。物忘れを防ぐのは会社の主張で、否定された。買い物のリストはほかの作業の例で、生かされなかった。15年は主張がされた時期で、上達が続いた期間ではない。

questions.question: What did the researchers conclude from the long-term study?
choices: The games raised players' general intelligence after all.
Practicing one particular skill had a real-world benefit.
The companies' original claims had been correct.
Older adults should avoid driving long distances.
questions.explanation: 長期の研究では、素早く反応するトレーニングが「fewer car accidents years later」と関係し、「the benefit came not from becoming smarter in general, but from improving a specific skill used in driving」と結論づけている。特定の能力を鍛えたことが実生活で役立ったので、正解はその言い換え。全般的な知能が上がった、という点ははっきり否定されている。会社の当初の主張は誤解を招く広告とされた。高齢者は運転を避けるべきだとは言っていない。

title: Singing to help stroke patients speak

questions.question: Why can some stroke patients sing words they cannot say?
choices: They practiced the songs before their strokes.
Singing relies on brain areas that often stay healthy.
Singing slows down the speed of their speech.
Familiar songs repair the damaged parts of the brain.
questions.explanation: 「singing uses areas of the brain that are often not damaged by a stroke」と述べている。歌うときは傷つかないことが多い脳の部分を使うので、正解はその言い換え。脳卒中の前に練習した、話す速さが遅くなる、という話はない。歌が傷ついた部分を治すとは言っていない(歌は傷ついていない部分を使う)。

questions.question: Why are some hospitals testing group classes?
choices: Patients enjoy singing with other people more.
Group classes produced better results in trials.
Patients find one-on-one sessions stressful.
Individual sessions take up too much therapist time.
questions.explanation: 「The method requires many hours of one-on-one sessions, however, so some hospitals are now testing group singing classes」と述べ、集団の教室は「allow one therapist to work with several patients」。一対一では療法士の時間がかかりすぎるので、正解はその言い換え。ほかの人と歌うほうが楽しい、集団のほうが結果がよかった、一対一がストレスになる、という話はない(試験で改善したのは一対一の方法)。

questions.question: How do deposit systems work?
choices: Buyers get an extra fee back for returning containers.
Shops pay people for recycling bottles at home.
Factories pay a tax on every bottle they make.
Drinks are sold only in glass bottles that can be reused.
questions.explanation: 「they pay a small extra charge ... and they get the money back when they return the empty container」と述べている。追加で払った料金が容器を返すと戻るので、正解はその言い換え。家でのリサイクルにお金を払う、工場への税、ガラス瓶だけで売る、という話はない。

questions.question: What do some small store owners say?
choices: Customers seldom bring bottles back to small shops.
Handling returned bottles keeps their workers too busy.
The extra charge on drinks should be made higher.
The government should pay for their recycling.
questions.explanation: 「some small store owners say that collecting and storing empty bottles takes up too much of their staff's time」と述べている。返却されたボトルの扱いで従業員が忙しくなりすぎるので、正解はその言い換え。客がボトルを返さない、追加料金を上げるべき、政府が払うべき、という話はない。

questions.question: Why did the number of thatching craftspeople decrease?
choices: There was less demand for their work.
Thatched roofs began to last much longer.
Farmers stopped growing grass for roofs.
Young people were not allowed to train.
questions.explanation: 「As fewer and fewer people lived in such houses, the number of craftspeople who could do the work fell sharply」と述べている。かやぶきの家に住む人が減り、仕事の需要が減ったので、正解はその言い換え。屋根は「every twenty to thirty years」でふき替えが必要で、長持ちするようになったのではない。農家はアシを集めていた人で、草を育てるのをやめたという話はない。今は若者向けの講習が開かれている。

questions.question: What is one problem thatchers face today?
choices: Protected buildings must use modern materials.
Suitable materials are hard to find nearby.
Training courses cost too much for villages.
Farmers refuse to sell reeds to them.
questions.explanation: 「many reed beds have disappeared, so some thatchers now have to bring in materials from abroad」と述べている。地元で材料が手に入りにくいので、正解はその言い換え。保護された建物は「traditional materials」を使わなければならず、現代の材料ではない。講習の費用、農家が売らない、という話はない。

title: Undersea internet cables as earthquake sensors

questions.question: What is one advantage of the new method?
choices: It does not need new devices on the seafloor.
It measures earthquakes on land more accurately.
It makes internet connections between continents faster.
It was developed by cable companies themselves.
questions.explanation: 海底の機器は「placing and maintaining them there is extremely expensive」なので少ない。新しい方法は「something that is already in place」、つまり既存のケーブルを使う。2つをつなぐと、海底に新しい機器を置かなくてよいことが利点になる。陸の地震、通信の速さの話はない。ケーブル会社はデータの提供に消極的な側で、開発したのではない。

questions.question: Why are cable companies reluctant to share their data?
choices: They would have to stop carrying internet data.
The first tests failed to detect any earthquakes.
They think it could put their cables in danger.
They want scientists to pay for the information.
questions.explanation: 「they worry that information about the cables' exact routes could help people damage them」と述べている。経路が分かるとケーブルが壊される危険があると考えているので、正解はその言い換え。通信を止める、料金を求める、という話はない。最初の試験では「it detected several earthquakes」と地震を捉えている。

title: A river dam that was lowered instead of removed

questions.question: What happened to the dam in the end?
choices: It was taken away completely to help the salmon.
It was kept as it was so the lake could be used.
It was repaired to supply power to the mill again.
It was made lower, and a route for fish was added.
questions.explanation: 完全な撤去は住民の反対で「the plan was put on hold」となった。最終的には「engineers lowered it by half and built a fish ladder」と述べている。ダムを低くして魚の通り道を造ったので、正解はその言い換え。完全な撤去は保留になった案。ダムはそのままではなく半分に下げられた。製粉所は閉鎖されている。

questions.question: Why have salmon numbers increased slowly?
choices: The new fish ladder is too steep for most adult salmon.
Residents are still catching many salmon in the lake.
A change in water temperature is harming some young fish.
The smaller lake no longer has enough water for fish.
questions.explanation: 「the water flowing out of the shallower lake is warmer than before, and some young fish cannot survive in it」と述べている。湖が浅くなって水温が上がり、若い魚が育たないので、正解はその言い換え。魚道が急すぎる、住民がサケを捕っている、という話はない。湖は「smaller but can still be used」で、水が足りないとは言っていない。

questions.question: How does an octopus change color?
choices: By eating different kinds of food.
By making special cells larger or smaller.
By swimming into warmer water.
By growing a new layer of skin.
questions.explanation: 「By making these cells larger or smaller, an octopus can turn red, brown, or white」と述べている。正解は本文と同じ語。食べ物、温かい水、新しい皮膚の話はない。

questions.question: What is the most common reason octopuses change color?
choices: To find a partner.
To hide from enemies.
To keep their bodies warm.
To catch more food.
questions.explanation: 「The most common reason is to hide from enemies」と述べている。正解は本文と同じ語。相手を見つける、体を温める、えさを捕る、という話はない。

questions.question: How do teachers use school gardens?
choices: To grow food for the school lunches.
To raise money for school trips.
To support their science classes.
To give students a quiet place to rest.
questions.explanation: 「Teachers also use the gardens in science lessons」と述べている。理科の授業に使うので、正解はその言い換え。昼食の食材を育てる、旅行の資金集め、休む場所、という話はない(昼食は、畑で作業した児童が野菜を選ぶようになった場面で出てくる)。

questions.question: What problem do some schools have?
choices: Finding helpers during the summer break.
Getting students to eat any vegetables.
Paying for seeds and garden tools.
Finding land with enough sunlight.
questions.explanation: 「some schools have trouble finding volunteers to water the plants while students are away」と述べている。夏休みに手伝う人を見つけるのが難しいので、正解はその言い換え。児童が野菜を食べない、種や道具の費用、日当たりの良い土地の話はない。

title: Fashion brands selling their own used clothes

questions.question: What is one business reason for these programs?
choices: They allow companies to raise the price of their new clothes.
They attract buyers who usually find the brand too expensive.
They are required by new laws to protect the environment.
They lower the cost of making new clothes from cotton.
questions.explanation: 「It brings in younger shoppers who could not otherwise afford the brand」と述べている。ふだんは高くて買えない客を呼び込めるので、正解はその言い換え。新品の値上げ、綿から服を作る費用の話はない。環境は会社が挙げる理由だが、法律で求められているとは言っていない。

questions.question: What have several brands decided to do?
choices: Pass some of the work on to other businesses.
Stop accepting clothes in poor condition.
Check every returned item by hand themselves.
Sell used clothes at their original price.
questions.explanation: 「Several have decided to work with specialist companies that handle the cleaning and checking for them」と述べている。洗浄と点検を専門の会社に任せるので、正解はその言い換え。状態の悪い服を断るという話はない。手で確かめる作業は外の会社に任せることにしたもの。古着は「about half the original price」で売っている。

title: Letting roadside grass grow for insects

questions.question: Why are roadsides valuable to bees and butterflies?
choices: They offer a place to live as other areas disappear.
Passing cars help to spread the seeds of flowers.
The grass there is cut short several times a year.
Farmers have planted wildflowers along the roads.
questions.explanation: 草を伸ばすと道ばたが「important homes for bees and butterflies」になり、その虫は「farmland and meadows have been turned into housing」で減ってきたと述べている。2つをつなぐと、ほかのすみかが失われる中で暮らす場所になるからだと分かる。年に何度も刈るのは以前のやり方で、それをやめたので虫のすみかになった。車が種を運ぶ、農家が植えた、という話はない。

questions.question: How have several towns responded to drivers' complaints?
choices: They have gone back to cutting all roadsides often.
They have put up signs to warn drivers about insects.
They have moved the wildflowers away from corners.
They keep the grass short only where roads meet.
questions.explanation: 運転手は角の背の高い草で車が見えにくいと苦情を言い、町は「leave the grass long along straight sections of road but continue to cut it short near crossings」と対応している。道が交わる場所だけ短く刈るので、正解はその言い換え。すべての道ばたを何度も刈るやり方には戻していない。警告の看板、野草を移す、という話はない。

title: A village dance younger than people believed

questions.question: What did the historian discover?
choices: The dance was a fairly recent creation.
The dance was even older than people thought.
The village's records had been lost in 1890.
Tourist guides had made up the dance's name.
questions.explanation: 500年以上前からと信じられていたが、「The dance did not appear in any records before 1890」で、手紙から「a local schoolteacher had created it」と分かった。比較的新しく作られた踊りなので、正解はその言い換え。もっと古いという話ではない。1890年は記録に初めて出てくる時期で、記録がなくなった年ではない。ガイドが名前を作ったという話はない。

questions.question: What is true about the village today?
choices: Most villagers still reject the historian's findings.
Fewer tourists come to see the dance each year.
The dance is no longer part of the festival.
It openly explains how the dance began.
questions.explanation: 初めは発見を受け入れない村人もいたが、「Today, however, the village tells the teacher's story on its festival website」と述べている。今は踊りの始まりを隠さず紹介しているので、正解はその言い換え。受け入れなかったのは「At first」の話。観光客は「have actually risen」で増えている。今も祭りのウェブサイトで紹介されており、踊りをやめたという話はない。

title: Collecting rainwater at home in cities

questions.question: Why do some city governments help pay for rain barrels?
choices: They make gardens grow faster.
They lower the use of tap water.
They keep streets clean after storms.
They let people wash cars for free.
questions.explanation: 「Some city governments now help pay for these barrels because they reduce how much tap water people use during dry summers」と述べている。水道水を使う量が減るからなので、正解はその言い換え。庭の植物が早く育つ話はない。嵐のときに役立つのは冠水を減らすことで、道路をきれいにする話ではない。洗車はたるの水の使い道の例で、補助の理由ではない。

questions.question: What do experts say about rain barrels?
choices: They should be emptied after storms.
They must be kept away from drains.
They should not be used for gardens.
They need to have a cover.
questions.explanation: 「experts warn that the barrels must be covered, because open water can attract mosquitoes」と述べている。ふたが必要なので、正解はその言い換え。嵐の後に水を捨てる、排水溝から離して置く、庭に使ってはいけない、という話はない。

title: Drones that carry medicine to remote islands

questions.question: What was one problem with sending medical items by boat?
choices: Blood samples were often damaged on the way.
Boats were able to carry only small loads.
Trips often could not be made in bad weather.
Hospitals had to pay high prices for fuel.
questions.explanation: 「trips were often canceled when the sea was rough」と述べている。海が荒れると運べなかったので、正解はその言い換え。検体が傷む、燃料費が高い、という話はない。小さな荷物しか運べないのはドローンのほうで、大きな物資は今も船で運ぶ。

questions.question: What is one benefit of using drones?
choices: Islanders no longer hear noise from boats.
Hospital beds can now be delivered quickly.
Small clinics no longer need their own doctors.
Patients are able to start treatment earlier.
questions.explanation: 「Blood test results now come back on the same day, so patients can begin treatment sooner」と述べている。患者が早く治療を始められるので、正解はその言い換え。音の苦情はドローンについてで、船の音がなくなったという話ではない。病院のベッドは今も船で運ぶ。診療所に医師が要らなくなる話はない。

questions.question: According to supporters, why do the fridges help people who have little money?
choices: Charities have stopped giving away food.
They can get food without feeling ashamed.
Nearby shops lower their prices for them.
They are paid to look after the fridges.
questions.explanation: 支持する人たちは「people who are struggling financially feel less embarrassed taking food from a fridge than asking for help at a charity」と言っている。慈善団体に頼むより恥ずかしさを感じずに食べ物を得られるので、正解はその言い換え。慈善団体が食べ物を配るのをやめた、店が値下げする、という話はない。冷蔵庫の世話をするのはボランティアで、報酬の話はない。

questions.question: How have some cities responded to health concerns?
choices: By banning community fridges on public streets.
By limiting what may be left and training volunteers.
By requiring shops to check the fridges every day.
By allowing only packaged food from charities.
questions.explanation: 市は「Rather than banning the fridges」と禁止はせず、「created rules, such as not allowing raw meat」と「offer training to the volunteers」の2つで対応した。入れてよい物を制限し、ボランティアに研修を行うので、正解は2つをまとめた言い換え。禁止は否定された対応。毎日確認するのはボランティアで、店ではない。慈善団体の包装された食品だけを認める話はない。

questions.question: How have several chains dealt with losses at self-checkouts?
choices: By putting more cameras near the machines.
By replacing nearly all staffed checkouts.
By letting only small purchases go through the machines.
By asking older shoppers to use the cashiers.
questions.explanation: カメラを増やす対応は「this did little to reduce their losses」と効果がなく、「Instead, several chains now allow only customers buying ten items or fewer to use the machines」と方針を変えた。少ない買い物だけを機械に通すので、正解はその言い換え。カメラは効果がなかった対応。店員のレジをほぼすべて置き換えるのは、やめた元の計画。高齢の客は人と話すのを好むという話で、店員のレジを使うよう頼んでいるのではない。

questions.question: What is suggested about the plan to replace almost all staffed checkouts?
choices: It succeeded in lowering theft in stores.
Some chains have moved away from it.
It was most popular with older customers.
It required one employee for each machine.
questions.explanation: ほぼすべてを置き換える計画のあと、「a number of these chains have changed course」と述べ、今は大きな買い物を店員のレジに通している。計画から離れたチェーンがあると分かるので、正解はその言い換え。盗難は増えたので、減らしたのではない。高齢の客は人と話すほうを好む。1人で何台も見られるのが利点とされていた。

questions.question: What is one advantage of electric buses?
choices: They make less noise.
They are cheaper to buy.
They can travel farther.
They carry more passengers.
questions.explanation: 「They are also much quieter」と述べている。音が静かなので、正解はその言い換え。電気バスは「cost more to buy」で、安くはない。走れる距離や乗れる人数の話はない。

questions.question: What are some cities doing to save money?
choices: Building fewer bus depots.
Replacing their buses gradually.
Using diesel buses only at night.
Raising the price of bus tickets.
questions.explanation: 「some cities are changing their buses a few at a time instead of all at once」と述べている。数台ずつ替えているので、正解はその言い換え。車庫を減らす、夜だけディーゼルバスを使う、運賃を上げる、という話はない。

questions.question: According to supporters, why are open-book exams useful?
choices: They make students think about how to use ideas.
They help students memorize more facts.
They reduce the time teachers spend grading.
They let students bring their own notes.
questions.explanation: 支持する人たちは、こうした試験が「understand ideas rather than memorize facts」を促し、問題は「apply what they have learned to new problems」を求めると言う。学んだことをどう使うかを考えさせるので、正解はその言い換え。事実の暗記は、この試験が重視しないもの。採点の時間の話はない。使ってよいのは教科書で、ノートは普通の試験で使えないものとして出てくる。

questions.question: Why do some students get lower scores on open-book exams?
choices: They do not study enough beforehand.
They feel too anxious during the test.
Their textbooks do not contain the answers.
The questions are too different from the lessons.
questions.explanation: 「some students prepare less for them and end up with lower scores, because they expect to find the answers during the test」と述べている。前もって十分に勉強しないので、正解はその言い換え。生徒はこの試験の前は「less anxious」で、不安が強いのではない。教科書に答えがない、という話はない。問題は学んだことを新しい問題に当てはめるもので、授業と違いすぎるという話ではない。

title: Treating hospital patients in their own homes

questions.question: Why can home treatment be good for older patients?
choices: They can see their doctors in person every day.
Nurses train their families before they go home.
They no longer have to take any medicine.
They avoid problems that often develop in hospitals.
questions.explanation: 自宅の患者は「less likely to become confused or lose strength」で、それは「common problems among older people in hospital beds」だと述べている。2つをつなぐと、入院中によく起こる問題を避けられると分かる。毎日来るのは看護師で、医師はビデオで確認する。家族が「not prepared」と言う人もいるので、研修を受けているという話ではない。薬は家族が飲ませることが多い。

questions.question: What do critics say about the programs?
choices: They put unexpected burdens on patients' relatives.
They reduce the number of beds for emergencies.
The devices often send incorrect results.
Nurses do not visit the patients often enough.
questions.explanation: 批判する人たちは、家族が「end up doing tasks such as giving medicine」になり、「not prepared for this responsibility」と言う人もいると指摘している。家族に思ってもいなかった負担がかかるので、正解は2つをまとめた言い換え。この取り組みは救急のためにベッドを「free up」するので、減らすのではない。機器の誤り、看護師の訪問が少ない、という話はない。

questions.question: What do recent studies suggest about the idea that stripes confuse lions?
choices: It explains why lions avoid zebras.
It was proved by tests on horses.
It also explains how zebras keep cool.
It is probably not correct.
questions.explanation: ライオンを混乱させる説と涼しく保つ説について「studies in recent years have found little support for either idea」と述べ、ライオンは「hunt zebras as successfully as they hunt other animals」と続けている。正しくない可能性が高いので、正解はその言い換え。ライオンがシマウマを避けるという話はない。馬の実験はハエについての説を支えるもの。涼しく保つのは別の説で、それも裏付けられていない。

questions.question: What did the experiment with horses show?
choices: Flies were not attracted to stripes at all.
Horses in plain coats stayed cooler.
Scientists learned why stripes work.
Stripes made it hard for insects to land.
questions.explanation: しま模様の馬には「far fewer flies landed on them」で、ハエは「seemed unable to slow down properly to land」だった。しまがあると虫が止まりにくいので、正解はその言い換え。ハエは「flew toward the striped horses」ので、まったく寄ってこなかったのではない。無地の馬が涼しかった、という話はない。理由は「still do not know exactly」とまだ分かっていない。

questions.question: What do supporters say about many sixteen-year-olds?
choices: They spend too much time online.
They can drive a car in most countries.
They already work and pay taxes.
They are better at using computers.
questions.explanation: 支持する人たちは「many sixteen-year-olds already work and pay taxes」と言い、だから政府のお金の使い方に意見を言えるべきだとしている。正解は本文と同じ言葉。インターネットの使いすぎ、車の運転、パソコンの得意さの話はない。

questions.question: What do some people worry about?
choices: Voting stations will become too crowded.
They may simply follow their parents' opinions.
They may vote by phone instead of in person.
Their teachers may tell them how to vote.
questions.explanation: 心配する人は「sixteen-year-olds may simply follow their parents' opinions」と言っている。正解は本文と同じ言葉。投票所の混雑、電話での投票、先生が投票先を指示する、という話はない。

title: Writing about worries before an exam

questions.question: According to psychologists, why do some students do poorly on exams?
choices: Anxiety uses up the brain's capacity for thinking.
They sit quietly instead of reviewing their notes.
They spend too many hours studying the night before.
They write their answers down too slowly.
questions.explanation: 心理学者は「worrying takes up the mental space that students need for solving problems」と考えている。不安が考えるための頭の余裕を使ってしまうので、正解はその言い換え。静かに座っていたのは研究の一方のグループで、成績が悪い理由として出てきたのではない。勉強のしすぎや、答えを書く速さの話はない。

questions.question: What did the researchers find?
choices: The method did not help students who were unprepared.
Anxious students gained the least from writing.
Sitting quietly was as useful as writing.
Writing about feelings can replace studying.
questions.explanation: 研究者は「the method is not a replacement for preparation」と注意し、「Students who had not studied did not benefit」と述べている。準備していない学生には効果がなかったので、正解はその言い換え。不安の強い学生ほど「especially」得点が上がったので、効果が最も小さかったのではない。書いたグループのほうが「scored noticeably higher」。勉強の代わりにはならないと言っている。

title: Using microphones to check soil health

questions.question: Why did the researchers try using microphones?
choices: Insects cannot be seen without special equipment.
The usual method is slow and harms what it studies.
Farmers asked for a faster way to dig up samples.
The sounds of worms were damaging local crops.
questions.explanation: ふつうの方法は「takes a great deal of time」で、さらに「disturbs the very creatures being studied」と述べている。2つをまとめると、時間がかかり、調べる生き物を傷つけてしまうので、正解はその言い換え。特別な道具が要るという話はない。農家は将来の利用者として出てくるだけで、掘る方法を頼んだのではない。ミミズの音が作物を傷めるという話はない。

questions.question: What is one limitation of the method?
choices: It cannot yet tell which creatures made the sounds.
It only works in soil that has been cleared.
The recordings are too costly for most farmers.
Restored soil is too quiet to be recorded well.
questions.explanation: 研究者は「most underground sounds have not yet been matched to particular species」で、「a recording cannot show exactly which animals are present」と認めている。どの生き物の音かまだ分からないので、正解はその言い換え。録音は再生された森と切り払われた場所の両方で行った。録音は「quickly and cheaply」調べる手段として期待されている。再生された森の土は「much louder」だった。

title: Companies that dropped and then revived employee ratings

questions.question: Why did some companies bring back ratings?
choices: Workers felt judged during the frequent conversations.
The conversations took managers several weeks to prepare.
Managers found it hard to justify differences in pay.
Employees asked to receive scores from one to five again.
questions.explanation: 企業は評価がないと「managers had trouble explaining why one employee received a larger pay raise than another」と気づき、「As a result」評価を戻した。昇給の差を説明しにくかったので、正解はその言い換え。裁かれていると感じたのは点数についてで、面談についてではない。何週間もかかったのは評価の準備。社員が点数を求めたという話はない。

questions.question: What is true about these companies now?
choices: They rate staff for pay and hold talks about growth.
They no longer hold frequent conversations with staff.
They give yearly ratings for every kind of decision.
They rate employees only on their skill development.
questions.explanation: 戻した評価は「only for decisions about pay」に使い、面談は「were kept」で、今は「mainly to discuss how employees can develop their skills」に使われている。給与には評価を、成長には面談を使っているので、正解はその内容。面談はやめていない。評価はすべての決定ではなく給与だけに使う。能力の伸ばし方は面談で話し合うもので、点数を付けるのではない。

title: Turning off street lights late at night

questions.question: Why are towns turning off street lights?
choices: To reduce crime on quiet roads.
To keep bats away from towns.
Because residents asked them to.
To cut their energy costs.
questions.explanation: 町は「this saves a large amount of electricity and money」と言っている。電気代を減らせるので、正解はその言い換え。犯罪は増えていないという研究はあるが、犯罪を減らすために消すのではない。コウモリは明かりで混乱するので助けになると言っていて、遠ざけるためではない。住民の一部はむしろ不安だと言っている。

questions.question: What have some towns decided to do?
choices: Turn the lights off all night.
Make the lights less bright.
Hire more police officers.
Move the lights to busy roads.
questions.explanation: 一部の町は「use dimmer lights instead of turning them off completely」と決めた。明かりを暗くするので、正解はその言い換え。消すのは真夜中から朝5時までで、一晩中ではない。警察官を増やす、街灯を移す、という話はない。

questions.question: Why did Allen Lane start selling paperbacks?
choices: He wanted good books to be cheap enough to buy.
He wanted libraries to lend more of his books.
He owned several stores in train stations.
He hoped to sell more packs of cigarettes.
questions.explanation: レーンは駅で良い読み物が見つからず「he decided to sell quality books at the same price as a pack of cigarettes」とした。良い本を買いやすい値段にしたかったので、正解はその言い換え。図書館は、本が高くて人々が借りるしかなかったという話で出てきた。駅に店を持っていたとは言っていない。たばこは値段のたとえで、たばこを売りたかったのではない。

questions.question: What did other publishers think about Lane's idea?
choices: His books were too large for coat pockets.
Low-priced books would not be profitable.
Books should be sold only in bookstores.
Hard covers were becoming too costly to make.
questions.explanation: ほかの出版社は「they thought such cheap books could never make money」と考えていた。安い本では利益が出ないと思っていたので、正解はその言い換え。レーンの本は「small enough to fit in a coat pocket」。書店だけで売るべきだという意見や、ハードカバーの製作費の話はない。

questions.question: According to researchers, why do fast eaters often eat too much?
choices: They spend twenty minutes choosing what to eat.
They feel less satisfied after eating smaller meals.
Their stomachs send signals faster than other people's.
Their brains learn too late that they have eaten enough.
questions.explanation: 研究者は「It takes about twenty minutes for the stomach to send signals to the brain that it is full」と言い、早食いの人は「finish a large meal before these signals arrive」と説明している。満腹だと脳が知るのが遅れるので、正解はその言い換え。20分は信号が届くまでの時間で、料理を選ぶ時間ではない。実験では量が減っても「just as satisfied」だった。信号が速く届くのではなく、届く前に食べ終えてしまう。

questions.question: What do some experts suggest?
choices: Workers should put down their forks between bites.
People should eat ten percent less at lunch.
Companies should ban eating at office desks.
Employers should allow workers longer meal breaks.
questions.explanation: 一部の専門家は「companies should give employees enough time to eat without hurrying」と提案している。会社が食事の時間を十分に与えるべきだという内容なので、正解はその言い換え。フォークを置くのは実験で参加者に頼んだことで、専門家の提案ではない。1割少なく食べたのは実験の結果。机で食べることを禁じる話はない。
